【18】Discussion

【19】The electrodiagnostic examination is very helpful in establishing the diagnosis and can help in differentiating the type of GBS. F-Wave examination as a preliminary examination in patients with GBS has been reported to establish the diagnosis . In this study， F-wave was absent in 4 participants and prolonged F-wave latency in 6 participants， with a mean value of 71.4 m/s. Besides being able to establish the diagnosis of GBS， F-wave examination in the acute phase can also determine the prognosis of GBS patients. The absence of F-waves indicates an inactive muscle that can be obtained in both demyelinating and axonal types of cases . However， in a study conducted in 2014 with70 GBS patients， prolonged F-wave latency was found only in demyelinating types and not in axonal type . The absence of F-waves is also identified by the inactivity of a muscle， which is related to the degree of motor weakness in patients with GBS.

【20】Conclusion

【21】An abnormal F-wave result can help to diagnose Guillain-Barre Syndrome in the acute phase， which sometimes does not show conduction block.

【0】Background：

【1】Bladder cancer (BC) is the second most common cancer involving the urinary system. In non-muscle-invading BC， transurethral resection of a bladder tumor followed by intravesical immunotherapy with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is the usual treatment. Disseminated (or systemic) BCG infection (BCGitis) represents the most severe adverse effect of intravesical BCG therapy， presenting with high-grade fever， with or without symp-toms in the urinary tract， leading to severe sepsis and death if left untreated. The treatment of choice con-sists of isoniazid， rifampicin， and ethambutol (with or without corticosteroids) for 6 months， and the recovery rate is extremely high. Given the fact that these drugs are hepatotoxic， treating a patient with liver cirrhosis is challenging.

【2】Case Report： We present a patient with a medical history of BC treated with transurethral resection and intravesical BCG therapy， presenting with fever， transaminasemia， and generalized weakness. Liver and bone marrow biopsies revealed liver cirrhosis and granulomas in both organs. A diagnose of BCGitis was made and the patient was treated with isoniazid， rifampicin， and ethambutol； rifampicin was substituted with moxifloxacin after 1 month due to worsening of liver laboratory results， and moxifloxacin was substituted with levofloxacin later on due to tonic-clonic seizures. The patient was treated for 4 more months with levofloxacin and for 7 more months with isoniazid and ethambutol， with no other adverse effects， preserving liver function and achieving cure of BCGitis.

【3】Conclusions： We present the case of a cirrhotic patient presenting with fever and deterioration of liver laboratory results， found to have BCGitis， and discuss possible difficulties in diagnosing and treating such patients.

【4】Keywords： BCG and Salmonella Infection， Disseminated ·lsoniazid·Liver Cirrhosis·Rifampin Bladder cancer (BC) is the ninth most common malignancy worldwide and the second most common one involving the urinary system； however， in middle-aged and elderly men， BC is the second most common malignancy， after only prostate cancer . The majority (75-80%) of BCs are non-muscle-invasive (NMIBC) and the treatment strategy includes trans-urethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT)， usually followed by intravesical immunotherapy with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin(BCG)， which is an attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bo-vis， leading to eradication of residual tumor， delay of disease progression， reduction in need for cystectomy， and prolong-ing survival .

【5】Despite the efficacy of intravesical BCG therapy， most patients report local， mild， early complications after instillation， like cys-titis (81%)， macroscopic hematuria (15%)， and urination fre-quency . Although BCG therapy is usually well-tolerat-ed， local and systemic complications can occur . Local complications involve the genitourinary tract in the form of epididymitis and granulomatous prostatitis， while systemic ones include short-term fever in 5-30% of patients， as well as allergic reactions， reactive arthritis， drug-induced liver injury， granulomatous hepatitis， and nephritis， all with a prevalence of less than 1%.

【6】Disseminated (or systemic) BCG infection (BCGitis) is the most severe adverse effect of intravesical BCG therapy. BCGitis has an incidence of 3% to 7% and presents with high-grade fever and/or various organ involvement with or without symptoms from the urinary tract， leading to severe sepsis and death if left untreated . BCGitis should be suspected in any patient who develops moderate-to-severe genitourinary or systemic symptoms following 21 instillation of intraves-ical BCG when no alternative diagnosis can be established. Microbiological documentation of the infection is required for definitive diagnosis； however， it has low sensitivity， and when histopathology is available， granulomas are commonly found. Due to the aforementioned difficulties， empirical treat-ment is commonly started upon suspicion； in this setting， im-provement of symptoms after treatment initiation is manda-tory for establishing the diagnosis . The treatment of choice for BCGitis consists of isoniazid， rifampicin， and eth-ambutol (alone or in combination with corticosteroids) for 6months， and the recovery rate is extremely high . Unfortunately， all of the above-mentioned drugs are hepato-toxic and can cause liver dysfunction， a problem most often encountered in cirrhotic patients . Here， we report the first case of a cirrhotic patient diagnosed with BCGitis with liver and bone marrow involvement， and we discuss potential therapeutic challenges related to the co-existence of BCGitis and liver cirrhosis.

【7】A 62-year-old non-smoker， male patient was admitted to Laiko General Hospital in Athens， Greece， due to a 6-month history of fever and generalized weakness. He had a medical history of non-muscle-invading BC， diagnosed 2 years before presenta-tion and treated with transurethral resection (TURBT) followed by 6 weeks of intravesical therapy with BCG. His medical an-amnesis was also notable for coronary artery disease and dys-lipidemia. He reported consuming moderate amounts of alco-hol daily for the past 20 years， stopping about 4 months ago.

【8】Approximately 2 months before presentation， the patient was hospitalized in another hospital due to fever up to 38.5C，ane-mia， and generalized weakness. During his stay there， a cys-toscopy was performed that revealed BC recurrence and he re-ceived a second course of 6 weekly intravesical BCG infusions. His fever was attributed to BC recurrence， so no further di-agnostic evaluation was performed at that time. Due to fever persistence and generalized weakness after treatment com-pletion， he was admitted to our hospital for further evalua-tion and management.

【9】Upon admission， the patient had an axillary temperature of 37.5℃， a blood pressure of 110/80 mmHg， a heart rate of 93 beats per minute， an oxygen saturation of 89% on ambient air， and a re-spiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute. On physical examina-tion， he was mildly lethargic with no focal neurological deficits or signs. Lung auscultation revealed bilateral crackles and abdomen examination revealed hepato-splenomegaly with no pain during palpation. The rest of his clinical examination was unremarkable.

【10】Routine laboratory blood results showed mild pancytopenia， elevated serum gamma glutamyl-transferase (GGT) and alka-line phosphatase (ALP) levels， as well as mildly elevated serum C-reactive protein(CRP) aspartate (AST) and normal alanine (ALT) aminotransferases levels . Urinary testing revealed py-uria and mild hematuria，whereas the urine culture was sterile.

【11】A chest X-ray was performed that demonstrated bilateral pleu-ral fluid accumulation，while abdominal ultrasound revealed a cirrhotic liver， splenomegaly， and mild ascites. No focal hepatic lesions were found. Computed tomography (C/T) scans of the chest and abdomen confirmed the aforementioned findings， without revealing portal or hepatic veins thrombosis.

【12】Ascitic fluid analysis was consistent with portal hypertension-induced ascites (serum-to-ascites albumin gradient of 2.1 g/dl)， with no signs of infection or malignancy. Testing for hepati-tis B and hepatitis C infections， Leishmaniasis， Q fever， and Brucellosis were negative， as were anti-nuclear， anti-smooth muscle， and anti-mitochondrial antibodies in serum. Serum iron studies， ferritin， ceruloplasmin level， and 24-h urine copper excretion were within normal limits. Quantiferon testing was negative and an echocardiogram was also normal.

【16】Due to pancytopenia， a bone marrow biopsy was performed. Additionally， a liver biopsy was performed due to progressive deterioration of liver biochemistry results. The bone marrow biopsy revealed non-caseating granulomas and Langhans giant cells ， whereas the liver biopsy showed bridg-ing fibrosis along with multiple， small， non-caseating granulo-mas and mild portal and lobular inflammation .

【17】Given the recent history of intravesical BCG therapy and the histological findings of liver and bone marrow biopsies， a di-agnosis of BCGitis was made. The patient was started on iso-niazid， rifampicin， and ethambutol， had a rapid resolution of symptoms， and was discharged from the hospital 4 days af-ter treatment initiation.

【18】One month after discharge， the patient had further deterio-ration of GGT and ALP serum levels ， so rifampicin was discontinued and moxifloxacin was initiated instead. Four weeks after treatment modification， the patient experienced an episode of loss of consciousness with gaze fixation that resolved spontaneously a few minutes later. A brain magnet-ic resonance imaging (MRI) was ordered， which revealed no pathology， and moxifloxacin was substituted for levofloxacin.

【19】During his next visits， the patient had a slow improvement of liver biochemistry and overall status， so levofloxacin was contin-ued for 4 additional months and isoniazid and ethambutol was continued for 7 additional months (9 months in total). Three months after treatment completion， the patient was afebrile， in good overall status， with normal levels of serum AST， ALT， and ALP， and only mildly elevated GGT levels， with no progression of liver cirrhosis status as defined by MELD and CTP scores.

【20】Discussion

【21】We present the case of a patient with a history of BC treated with intravesical BCG who was concurrently diagnosed with dis-seminated BCGitis (with bone marrow and liver involvement).

【22】BCGitis is a well-known adverse effect of intravesical BCG in fusions. Incorrect instillation of BCG with iatrogenic trauma or concurrent urinary infection， previous urinary interventions， and the presence of breaches in the bladder are the most common risk factors . Since the attenuated Mycobacterium bovis is a live strain preserving a degree of vir-ulence， instillation of BCG in a patient with immunosuppres-sion also carries a risk of BCGitis . In our case， the pa-tient was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis， a condition in which reduction in the reticuloendothelial system cell mass (Kupffer cells and sinusoidal endothelial cells) and porto-systemic shunts lead to immune system dysfunction， making BCGitis a possi-ble complication .

【23】BCGitis should be suspected in every patient having received intravesical BCG infusions， presenting with fever and/or or-gan involvement， with or without symptoms in the genitouri-nary tract. However， establishing the diagnosis can be quite challenging， needing， apart from the history of BCG expo-sure， exclusion of all other causes of fever， as well as clinical improvement after treatment initiation， since microbiologi-cal and/or histopathological documentation is rarely feasible. Nevertheless， in our patient， the clinical suspicion was sup-ported by liver and bone marrow histology， which found non-caseating granulomas. Interestingly， unlike tuberculosis， infec-tion with M. bovis leads to non-caseating granulomas . Moreover， Quantiferon testing is not helpful， since interferon-gamma release assays use stimulating antigens that are pres-ent in M. tuberculosis and pathogenic M. bovis strains but ab-sent in M. bovis BCG .

【24】Initial treatment for BCGitis consists of isoniazid， rifampicin， and ethambutol， alone or in combination with corticosteroids， for 6 months， and the infection usually resolves with no se-quelae. Corticosteroid use is controversial and is usually re-served for severe cases of miliary involvement and respiratory failure. Treating a cirrhotic patient poses many challenges， since anti-tuberculosis treatment is accompanied with signif-icant hepatotoxicity. Isoniazid is metabolized in the liver， lead-ing to hepatotoxic metabolites in the form of acetyl hydrazine and hydrazine， which cause hepatocellular steatosis and necro-sis ， with an incidence of 0.6% when used as mono-therapy ， although severe isoniazid-induced hepatotoxic-ity seems to be heavily under-reported . Rifampicin usually causes transient transaminitis that is thought to be benign； however， it has also been associated with centrilobular pa-renchymal necrosis and elevation of conjugated bilirubin due to cholestasis ， leading to a 4-fold higher incidence of hepatotoxicity when used in combination with isoniazid . Interestingly， according to Park et al， this incidence increases to 17% when a liver disease coexists， irrespective of the pres-ence or absence of cirrhosis . In contrast， ethambutol is not associated with clinically important hepatotoxic effects .

【25】Due to these adverse effects， treating a patient with liver cir-rhosis for BCGitis involves the risk of decompensation or even acute-on-chronic liver failure . According to WHO guide-lines， the number of hepatotoxic agents that can be used in a cirrhotic patient depends on the severity of liver disease . Regarding anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs， some authors propose the use of isoniazid and rifampicin for patients with Child-Pugh<7， isoniazid or rifampicin for Child-Pugh 8-10， and none of the hepatotoxic anti-TB drugs for patients with Child-Pugh≥11 . Since hepatotoxicity usually occurs during the first 2 months of treatment， close monitoring of transaminas-es'levels is mandatory in that period .

【26】Due to the aforementioned problems， our patient was started on isoniazid， rifampicin， and ethambutol， according to guide-lines. The patient had a deterioration of liver enzymes se rum levels during his first follow-up visit， so rifampicin was changed to moxifloxacin.

【27】With regards to fluoroquinolones (FQs)， which are the most commonly used second-line agents， a large case-control safe-ty study showed no significant association between moxiflox-acin and levofloxacin exposure and hepatotoxicity risk， while Ho et al found that introduction of FQ in patients with hepa-titis induced by first-line agents did not cause additional hep-atotoxicity . On the contrary， Paterson et al found in-creased risk of acute liver injury among older patients . Given these results， FQs may be a reasonable option in pa-tients with hepatitis after exposure to first-line anti-TB agents.

【28】Even though this regimen was considered to be safe for a cir-rhotic patient， our patient developed seizures attributed to moxifloxacin treatment， which resolved after discontinuation of the medication. Although levofloxacin， ofloxacin， and moxi-floxacin have the lowest potential of inducing central nervous system adverse events among the FQ available， case reports exist attributing episodes of seizures to moxifloxacin treat-ment . Our patient's regimen was once more changed and levofloxacin was initiated instead of moxifloxacin， with-out other significant toxicities.

【29】Although the usual treatment duration for BCGitis is 6 months， no treatment recommendations exist regarding immunocom-promised patients， since most data come from children with primary immunodeficiency syndromes for which regimens with various durations were used . In a case report present-ed by Winger et al ， a 16-year-old patient with systemic lupus erythematosus， diagnosed with intestinal M. bovis in-fection was treated for a total of 9 months， with symptoms resolution. We opted to use a commonly used 3-drug regimen for 6 months and prolonged isoniazid-ethambutol for 3 more months. The levofloxacin treatment was discontinued to di-minish the risk of hepatotoxicity.

【30】During his last visit， 3 months after treatment completion (12months after treatment initiation)， the patient was stable， with no fever or deterioration of cirrhosis status.

【31】Conclusions

【32】We report a unique case of concurrent diagnosis of BCGitis and liver cirrhosis in a patient with previous intravesical BCG administration for BC and discuss the difficulties in diagnos-ing and treating such a patient for BCGitis.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a discrete disorder defined as the loss of two or more clinically recognized pregnancies. The increasing incidence of RPL in recent days may be due to chromosomal and congenital abnormalities， antiphospholipid syndrome， uterine anomalies， hereditary thrombophilia， autoimmunity and environmental factors， but the cause of RPL still remains undetermined in the majority of cases. Folate deficiency is one of the causes of congenital abnormalities， which may lead to pregnancy losses. Any deficiency in the folate metabolic pathway leads to low levels of folate， which has been associated with abnormalities in both mothers (anaemia) and fetuses (congenital abnormalities). Also， it is associated with increased homocysteine levels which may contribute to these conditions. Objectives： Study folate metabolism status in RPL by correlating the association between 5，10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase gene (MTHFR) Data Sources： Data from Pubmed，EMBASE， MEDLINE and many other databases were searched. Similar strategies were applied for each article search. Study selection： the review was restricted to studies on recurrent pregnancy loss， Folate metabolism， MTHFR gene and study statistics. Results： A hypothesis was drawn from different studies. A positive link was observed in MTHFR gene alleles mutation， hyperhomocysteinaemia and recurrent pregnancy loss. Conclusion： Understanding the molecular genetics of folate metabolic pathway will provide newer avenues in effectively managing pregnancy losses due to low folate levels (in MTHFR gene polymorphism) with supplementation of folic acid or L-methylfolate.

【1】KEYWORDS genetic Variation， Folate metabolism， MTHFR

【2】Introduction

【3】The magnitude of the problem： About 10-15% of all clinically recognized pregnancies end in a miscarriage globally. It has been reported that the recurrence risk increases with each suc-cessive pregnancy loss. The risk of pregnancy loss in women with atleast one live born infant without any prior fetal loss is12% for the next pregnancy； whereas recurrence risk for those with at least one， two and three prior fetal loss is 24， 26 and 32% respectively and 40-45% with no live born and with 2 or more fetal loss.

【4】Folic acid and MTHFR：The 5， 10-methylenetetrahydrofolate re-ductase (MTHFR) gene is located on chromosome 1 at 1p36.3. The complementary DNA sequence is 2.2-kilo bases long and consists of 11 exons.MTHFR catalyses the conversion of5，10- methylenetetrahydrofolate into 5-methyltetrahydrofolate， the major circulating form of folate. Folic acid and MTHFR are involved in complex biochemical pathways . 5-methyltetrahydrofolate serves as a methyl donor for the remethylation of homocysteine to methionine， the precur-sor of S-adenosylmethionine(SAM). Lack of methyl group production results in an intracellular accumulation of S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) and an increase in plasma total homocysteine levels .

【5】In its 5-methyl form， Folate participates in single-carbon trans-fers that occur as part of the synthesis of nucleotides； the syn-thesis of S-adenosyl-methionine； the remethylation of homocys-teine to methionine； Normal MTHFR activity may help main-tain the pool of circulating folate and methionine and possibly prevent a buildup of homocysteine. It is also unclear how abnor-malities of folate metabolism would cause structural anomalies in the embryo， although both insufficient methylations of cru-cial metabolites and direct toxicity of homocysteine have been suggested as possible mediators of teratogenesis.C677T and A1298C are the two common MTHFR gene alleles and associ-ated with congenital anomalies， cardiovascular diseases， stroke， and coagulation abnormalities. The C677T allele is character-ized by a point mutation at position 677 of the MTHFR gene that converts a cytosine (C) into thymine (T)； this mutation re-sults in an amino acid substitution (alanine to valine) in the enzyme. People who are homozygous for the C677Tallele tend to have mildly increased blood homocysteine levels if their fo late intake is insufficient. In the A1298Callele， a point mutation in exon 7 results in an amino acid substitution (glutamate for alanine) in the enzyme. People who are homozygous for the A1298C allele do not appear to have higher serum homocys-teine levels than controls. However， people who are compound heterozygous for the A1298Cand C677Talleles (i.e.， people with the A1298CIC677Igenotype) tend to have a biochemical profile similar to that seen among C677Thomozygotes， with increased serum homocysteine levels and decrease serum folatelevels.

MTHFR gene mutation occurs there are no methyl group donors for the conversion of homocysteine to me-thionine， hence plasma homocysteine level increases which may cause endoplasmic reticulum stress or DNA damage； hence it may cause decreased vascularisation of the placenta or throm-botic disorder or congenital abnormalities which leads to fetal loss. As there is no conversion of homocysteine to methionine， S-adenosylmethionine will not produce， hence as it is an im-portant methyl donor for the reactions like DNA methylation， conversion of ethanolamine to choline etc. this leads to many congenital neural defects， which may lead to fetal loss.

【11】Discussion

【12】Subjects with homozygous (TT) for the C677T mutation had significantly greater plasma total homocysteine concentrations(P<0.01) than subjects without the mutation (CC). Homozygotes for the A1298C mutation did not have elevated plasma total ho-mocysteine concentrations. The exact mechanism for the cause of miscarriage in hyperhomocysteinaemia is unknown. The au-thor demonstrated defective vascularization of the chorionic villus in hyperhomocysteinaemia.

【13】Several observations suggest that the risk of neural tube de-fects associated with MTHFR genotypes may vary depending on nutritional status. For example， in one study， maternal vitamin use was associated with a reduced risk for spina bifida among both infants with normal alleles (OR=0.30) and those with the homozygous C677T genotype (OR=0.20). The child's risk of disease increased with C677Thomozygosity in the mother but not in the father is associated with Spina bifida in the in-fant3. The risk of pregnancy failure was significantly elevated only incarriers of the homozygous variant of both SNPs (677T/T and 1298C/C) and， interestingly， was seen in patients experienc-ing late (C677T) and combined early-late(C677T and A1298C. There was a higher prevalence of the 1298AC genotype and a lower prevalence of the 1298AA genotype in the spontaneous aborted embryos compared with the control group. Recent reports indicate that there is variation between different coun-tries and ethnic groups in the frequency of 677C-T mutation in the MTHFR geneThe prevalence of polymorphism of the MTHFR gene varies according to ethnic origin in E. It ranges from 23-37% in different European populations.

【14】Jewish population that the prevalence of A1298C is similar in frequency to the known C677T mutation. The allele frequency was 0.34 for the A1298C mutation and 0.37 for the C677T muta-tion. Approximately 10% of Caucasian and Asian popula-tions (homozygous TT) have 70% less activity in the enzymes needed to receive any benefit from folic acid. Another 40% of the population (heterozygous CT) appears to convert only a limited amount of folic acid into levomethylfolic acid. Therefore， they cannot fully process supplemental folic acid at RDA or higher dose levels. The remaining population does not have a known MTHFR polymorphism and can metabolize folic acid more efficiently. The percentage of allele frequency and ho-mozygosity were highest in the Italian population and lowest in the African population. Among Asians， the allele frequency and homozygosity were towards higher frequency. In north Indian population clearly showed the RPL positive association with MTHFR GENE mutation. The study concluded that6.3009-and 1.9591-fold increased homozygosity and heterozygosity of the MTHFR C677T polymorphism confer a risk of idiopathic RPL， respectively. The south Indian population showed six women in the study group， and two among the controls were found to be heterozygous for the C677T MTHFR mutation in 24 cases each. None were homozygous for the mutant (TT) allele.

【15】The mean incidence of the homozygous T/T genotype was14.5% of MTHFR gene mutation in mothers of children with neural tube defects， which was 8.5% in unmatched control sub-jects. MTHFR 677CT and TT genotypes appeared to be risk factors for conotruncal heart defects； hence neural crest cells are affected due to impaired folate and/or homocysteine metabolism interfering with developing heart. The mecha-nism by which MTHFR gene mutations lead to pregnancy loss is unknown. A logical hypothesis is that venous thrombosis leads to placental insufficiency due to endothelial damage from hyper-homocysteinemia. The study clearly indicates that homozy-gosity and heterozygosity for the MTHFR C677T polymorphism confer a 6.3009-and 1.9591-fold increased risk of idiopathic RPL， respectively. The majority of the study showed a positive B11association of RPL with MTHFR gene mutation. But a study in London disagrees with the positive relation between RPL& MTHFR gene mutation. They stated that the MTHFR gene polymorphism was not a predictive factor for RPL.

【16】Conclusion

【17】MTHFR gene mutation is an important gene polymorphism in folic acid metabolism， which is associated with recurrent pregnancy loss with normal or low folic acid levels. This gene regulates the MTHFR enzyme， which is necessary to convert5， 10 methylenetetrahydrofolates to 5-methyl tetrahydrofolate. Further 5-methyl tetrahydrofolate converts into tetrahydrofolate， which provides a methyl group for the transmethylation reaction in which homocysteine converts into methionine through the conversion of vitamin B12 to methylcobalamin. Identifying hy-perhomocysteinaemia in women with recurrent pregnancy loss may help in therapeutic normalization and permit normal birth. Hence this study hypothesises that the prevalence of MTHFR gene mutation in the south Indian population gives the burden of folic acid deficiency and its consequence as a fetal loss. So this study may help to provide information on an alternate form of folic acid (which cannot help in the metabolism of homocysteine) like L-methyl folate in MTHFR mutation and the need for fortifi-cation of food with folate. Moreover， these genes’ physiological state may help manage subsequent pregnancies. So， the mode of treatment is guided by the underlying cause of RPL.

【0】Background：

【1】We report 4 family members， a 29-year-old son， 54-year-old father，79-year-old grandmother， and 84-year-old grandfather， with COVID-19 pneumonia. Only the son had heart failure， with reduced ejection fraction and atri-al fibrillation. This report aims to show that age and baseline comorbidities are not always predictors of severe COVID-19 disease.

【2】Case Reports：

【3】Case 1： The son， a 29-year-old man， presented with dyspnea and palpitation. His nasopharyngeal swab was positive for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). He required high-flow nasal can-nula oxygen therapy and had new-onset atrial fibrillation and reduced ejection fraction. Case 2： The father， a54-year-old man， presented with dyspnea. Nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. He required reg-ular nasal cannula oxygen therapy. Electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm. Echocardiogram showed normal ejection fraction. Case 3： The grandfather， an 84-year-old man with a history of atrial flutter， chronic kidney dis-ease， and hypertension， presented with dyspnea and fever. Nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. He required regular nasal cannula oxygen therapy. Electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm. Echocardiogram showed normal ejection fraction. Case 4： The grandmother， a 79-year-old woman with a history of hyperten-sion， presented with dyspnea. Nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. She required regular nasal cannula oxygen therapy.Electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 is recognized to affect family members and can involve the heart， causing heart failure and cardiac arrhythmia like atrial fibrillation. This report highlights the importance of cardiac mon-itoring and consideration of cardiac damage， even without previous risk factors， in all hospitalized patients with COVID-19.

【6】Keywords： Atrial Fibrillation·COVID-19· Heart Failure， Systolic·Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2

【7】COVID-19 is caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) . It is a global pandemic dis-ease that affected more than 65 million people worldwide and more than 14 million in the United States as of December 3.2020， according to the Johns Hopkins coronavirus resource cen-ter . There have been more than 1.5 million global deaths related to COVID-19 .COVID-19 started in Wuhan， a city in the Hubei province of China， in December 2019 and then spread worldwide to affect 191 countries and regions . The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 as a pandem-ic on March 11， 20204.

【8】COVID-19 disease can affect many organs， including the heart， kidneys，liver， and lungs， and the hematological， nervous， and gastrointestinal systems， but it usually starts within the re-spiratory tract . Cardiac damage caused by COVID-19 can take multiple presentations， such as cardiac arrest， myocardi-tis， stress-induced cardiomyopathy， acute coronary syndrome， venous thromboembolism， arrhythmias， and subsequently heart failure . Baseline cardiovascular diseases put pa-tients with COVID-19 at a higher risk of increased complica-tions and death . Also， cardiac injury caused by COVID-19increases the risk of morbidities and mortalities . One of the most common conduction system diseases in patients with COVID-19 is atrial arrhythmia， such as atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter . There is a known association between atri-al fibrillation and SARS-CoV-2 infection . Atrial fibrillation can be the presenting symptom of COVID-19 in some cases or can be a complication during the course of the disease . Heart failure secondary to COVID-19 is yet to be studied at multiple levels， including epidemiology， mechanisms of inju-ry， risk factors， and management. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction was reported in patients with COVID-19 . Some studies have shown that preexisting comorbidities in el-derly patients are the main risk factors for cardiac injury from COVID-1915.

【9】Herein， we present 4 cases of members from the same fami-ly， including a 29-year-old son，54-year-old father，84-year-old grandfather， and 79-year-old grandmother， who were hospi-talized with COVID-19. Only the son had atrial fibrillation and heart failure， with reduced ejection fraction and without a pre-vious history of cardiovascular disease.

【10】COVID-19 testing in these patients was performed by viral RNA detection using a nasopharyngeal swab. Samples were tested by reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction(RT-PCR) methodology using the Bio-Fire COVID-19 test de-vice. This test was developed， and its performance character-istics were determined by Bio-Fire Defense， LLC (Salt Lake City， UT， USA). This test is authorized by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration under emergency use authorization (EUA) of in vitro diagnostic tests for the detection of SARS-CoV-2(EUA Number： EUA200044) . The specificity of most of the RT-PCR tests is 100%， but false-positive results can happen secondary to reagent contamination or technical errors . In our cases， the pretest probability， and the clinical/radiolo-gy findings with a positive RT-PCR SARS-CoV-2 test in a high COVID-19 prevalence area confirmed the COVID-19 diagnosis.

【11】Case Reports

【12】Case 1. The 29-Year-Old Son

【13】A 29-year-old man with no past medical history presented to the hospital in October 2020 with fever， chills， sweats， palpita-tion， and shortness of breath for 1 week before admission. In the Emergency Department (ED)， his vital signs showed a tem-perature of 38.05℃， blood pressure of 124/72 mmHg， heart rate of 131 beats per min， respiratory rate of 28 breaths per min， and oxygen saturation (SaO，) of 91% on room air. His body mass index was 34.7. The physical examination showed a young man with mild respiratory distress. The lung exami-nation showed diffuse rhonchi in both lungs， with decreased breath sounds at the bases bilaterally. The heart examination showed an irregularly irregular heart rate and rhythm. The physical examination was otherwise unremarkable.The labo-ratory examination showed a white blood cell (WBC) count of7.3 K (reference range， 4.8-10.8 K)， ferritin level of 807 ng/mL (range， 3-244 ng/mL)， B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) of 143pg/mL (range， 0-100 pg/mL)， C-reactive protein (CRP) level of13.3 mg/dL (range， 0-0.9 mg/dL)， erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 20 mm/h (range， 0-20 mm/h)， and troponin of0.062 ng/mL (range， 0-0.056 ng/mL)， which then normalized. The arterial blood gas had a pH of 7.46， PCO， of 26.5mmHg， and PaO， of 64.1 mmHg. The electrocardiogram (EKG) showed an irregularly irregular RR interval and no distinct P waves， consistent with atrial fibrillation . His heart rate， which was 155 beats per min initially， improved with in-travenous (i.v.) cardizem to 109 beats per min. The patient had a chest computed tomography (CT) scan with a pulmonary em-bolism protocol， which showed extensive bilateral ground-glass opacities and no evidence of a pulmonary embolism .

【16】His respiratory Bio-Fire panel using a nasopharyngeal swab was positive for SARS-CoV-2. He initially required only 2 L of O，us-ing a nasal cannula to keep his Sao， above 94%. However， his SaO， continued to drop to the high 80s even with a nasal can-nula， venti-mask， and non-rebreather mask.
