【0】Background：

【1】Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is a rare but fatal complication of hyperthyroidism that is induced by the hy-percoagulable state of thyrotoxicosis. Although it is frequently difficult to diagnose CVT promptly， it is impor-tant to consider it in the differential diagnosis when a hyperthyroid patient presents with atypical neurologic symptoms.

【2】Care Report：

【3】A 49-year-old Japanese female with unremarkable medical history came in with thyroid storm and multiple progressive ischemic stroke identified at another hospital. Treatment for thyroid storm with beta-blocker，glu-cocorticoid， and potassium iodide-iodine was started and MR venography was performed on hospital day 3for further evaluation of her progressive ischemic stroke. The MRI showed CVT， and anticoagulation therapy in addition to the anti-thyroid agents， was initiated. The patient's thyroid function was successfully stabilized by hospital day 10 and further progression of CVT was prevented.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Physicians should consider CVT when a patient presents with atypical course of stroke or with atypical MRI findings such as high intensity area in apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping. Not only is an early diag-nosis and initiation of anticoagulation important， but identifying and treating the underlying disease is essen-tial to avoid the progression of CVT.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Early Diagnosis · Intracranial Thrombosis · Thrombophilia·Thyroid Crisis·Venous Thrombosis Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is a rare but potentially fa-tal cerebrovascular complication of hyperthyroidism that is induced by the hypercoagulable state of thyrotoxicosis . The clinical manifestation of CVT differs greatly between cas-es and this makes the diagnosis difficult for clinicians . It is important to include CVT in the differential diagnosis and make further investigation when a hyperthyroid patient ap-pears with atypical neurologic symptoms and findings on im-ages . To avoid the progression of thrombosis， it is nec-essary to make early diagnosis and initiate anticoagulation as well as provide treatment for the underlying disease. Here， we describe a unique patient who presented with hyperthy-roid storm and progressive ischemic stroke caused by CVT.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 49-year-old Japanese female with an unremarkable medical history presented to an outside clinic with a one-month histo-ry of headaches， palpitations， diaphoresis， and weight loss. Her family history was not remarkable and the patient denied any history of tobacco smoking， heavy alcohol consumption， or sub-stance abuse. Subsequent laboratory investigations revealed TSH of <0.01 mlU/L， free T3 of 7.82 pg/dL， and free T4 of 2.48 ng/dL(normal range： TSH 0.5-5 mlU/L； free T3 2-4.48 pg/mL； free T4 0.84-1.70 ng/dl). She was diagnosed with hyperthyroid-ism， and methimazole was initiated as an outpatient therapy.

【9】Two days after the diagnosis， she started to have weakness in her left proximal upper extremity and left leg. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRl) of the brain showed cerebral in-farction in the right pre- and post-central gyri. She was ad-mitted to an outside hospital and started on intravenous arg atroban. During the next six days， she developed weakness in her right leg as well. On day 7， a second MRI showed new in-farctions in the left frontal lobe， posterior lobe， and right pa-rietal lobe . On day 8， she was noted to have confu-sion， tachypnea， tachycardia， hyperthermia， and hypertension. Based on Burch and Wartofsky scoring system ， the total score of her condition was 85 points and was highly sugges-tive of thyroid storm. She was transferred to our hospital for further evaluation and treatment.

【10】On admission to our hospital， although she did not have ap-parent diffuse goiter or orbitopathy， she was diagnosed with Graves' disease based on thyrotropin receptor antibodies posi-tivity  at 2.2 IU/L (normal range <2.0 IU/L). Thyroid function tests were as follows： TSH <0.005 mlU/L， free T3 8.10 pg/mL， free T4 4.41 ng/dL She was started on glucocorticoid，beta-blocker， potassium iodide-iodine， and methimazole for thyroid storm. As the patient had no atrial fibrillation and MR angiog-raphy of the brain revealed no occlusion， MR venography of the brain was performed on hospital day 3 to clarify the etiol-ogy of her repeated infarction. The venography showed throm-bosis in the left transverse sinus， sigmoid sinus， and internal jugular vein， confirming the diagnosis of cerebral venous si-nus thrombosis； intravenous heparin infusion was started.

【11】She underwent subsequent venous angiography and catheter thrombectomy with gradual clinical improvement. Her free T3and free T4 slowly improved， normalizing by day 10， and was followed by the successful discontinuation of corticosteroid and beta-blocker. Her neurological condition was improving and she was transferred to a rehabilitation hospital on day 85.

【12】Discussion

【13】Here， we describe a rare case of hyperthyroid storm associat-ed with progressive cerebral ischemia caused by CVT. Although cardioembolic stroke induced by thyrotoxic atrial fibrillation is well-recognized phenomenon， CVT has also been reported as a cerebrovascular complication of hyperthyroidism， due to the hypercoagulable state induced by thyrotoxicosis .CVT is a very uncommon disease with an estimated incidence be-tween 0.5% and 1% of all strokes in the general population and with a mortality rate of 5% to 30%. Clinical manifes-tations of CVT vary between cases depending on the under-lying disease and location of thrombosis， and this makes the timely diagnosis challenging . It is important to consider CVT among the differential diagnoses of a patient with hyperthy-roidism manifesting atypical neurologic symptoms and imag-ing findings such as bilateral progressive ischemic stroke， con-tinuous headache， or seizure. Early diagnosis of CVT and rapid initiation of anticoagulation， along with treatment of the un-derlying disease， can effectively halt thrombosis progression.

【14】Although hyperthyroidism is not a widely acknowledged risk factor for venous thrombosis， a possible association between thyrotoxicosis and venous thrombosis has been reported pre-viously . A case of thyroid storm complicated with dissem-inated intravascular coagulation (DIC) was also reported . CVT with thyrotoxicosis was described as early as 1927 by Doyle ； and previous studies suggest that thyrotoxicosis increases plasma levels of tissue factor， Factor VIII， Factor IX， von Willebrand Factor， fibrinogen， d-dimer， and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1.

【15】In addition to arterial ischemia， physicians should also consid-er CVT when a hyperthyroid patient presents with stroke； the venous pathophysiology of which is different from its arterial counterpart. Arterial infarction leads to cell membrane dam-age， causing cytotoxic brain injury and edema. In contrast， ve-nous sinus thrombosis and the associated impairment of ve-nous drainage can cause an increase in venous and capillary pressure. The increased intravenous pressure contributes to an increase in intravascular pressure and a lowering of cerebral perfusion pressure resulting in both vasogenic and cytotoxic edema . Due to this edema， clinical manifestations of CVT may differ widely depending on the underlying disease and location of thrombosis. In general， CVT-associated symptoms are grouped into three categories： isolated intracranial hyper-tension syndrome， focal syndrome， and encephalopathy . These multiple manifestations， which overlap with other com-mon diseases including primary headache， intracranial hemor-rhage， and arterial infarction， make it difficult for physicians to consider CVT in their differential diagnosis. As such， recog-nition of these imaging findings may play an important role in the rapid diagnosis of CVT.

【16】Imaging characteristics differ between arterial stroke and CVT. On MRI， cell membrane damage induced by hypoxic changes from arterial infarction manifests as hyperintensity in diffu-sion-weighted imaging (DWI) and hypointensity in the acute phase of apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping imag-es， which may evolve into hyperintensity after 10 days . In contrast， the increase in capillary pressure from CVT induces vasogenic edema， which manifests as hyperintensity in ADC mapping， and hypo-， iso-， or hyperintensity in DWI. Later， when increased venous pressure results in arterial malperfusion， ar-terial infarction will occur， typically manifesting as hyperinten-sity mixed with hypointensity in ADC mapping . Edematous changes and early phase hyperintensity in ADC mapping is characteristic in CVT and can assist in identifying an otherwise challenging diagnosis， with subsequent MR venography or CT venography performed for definitive diagnosis. In our case， we retrospectively reviewed the ADC mapping MRI performed on day 7 at the previous hospital， a few days after new mus-cle weakness developed. It demonstrated new hyperintensi-ty lesions， which did not exist in the first MRI . This was suggestive of venous sinus thrombosis rather than arte-rial stroke， and in retrospect， an evaluation of the venous si-nus may have been advised at this point.

【17】Delays in diagnosis of CVT are common and may lead to sig nificant morbidity. The median delay from onset of symptoms to hospital admission， as well as from symptom onset to di-agnosis， were reportedly four and seven days， respectively  Thrombosis progresses rapidly if left untreated， and we should consider CVT when patients with hyperthyroidism have atyp-ical imaging studies and neurologic findings. To prevent pro-gression of CVT， swift treatment with adequate anticoagulation is critical. Although anticoagulation during the acute phase of arterial stroke is usually not recommended due to hemorrhag-ic risk； however， it is strongly recommended， even in the acute phase， for venous sinus thrombosis . In addition to anti-coagulation therapy， it is necessary to identify and treat the underlying cause of thrombosis. As Factor VIII activity usually returns to normal after a few weeks of anti-thyroid therapy， correction of the hyperthyroid state was an important part of the treatment strategy for CVT in our case . An extensive search in all-language literature that identified all the case re-ports of CVT published from April 2005 up to December 2010found only 26 cases . In addition， there were 12 cases that reported on the relationship between hyperthyroidism and CVT. Although it is not common， physicians should be aware of hyperthyroidism as a potential cause of CVT. In order to prevent further deterioration of established thrombosis， it is essential not only to make rapid diagnosis of CVT and ini-tiate anticoagulation but also to treat the underlying disease such as hyperthyroidism.

【18】We reported here on a case of CVT associated with hypercoag-ulability of hyperthyroidism. Clinicians should consider venous sinus thrombosis when they encounter a stroke in a hyperthy roid patient and thyroid function tests should be checked for a cause of thrombosis. The hyperintensity or mixed intensity in ADC map can be helpful for the diagnosis of CVT.

【0】ABSTRACT Delirium is a serious and common acute neuropsychiatric syndrome in the elderly， characterized by disturbances in consciousness， memory， orientation， perception， thought， behaviour， fluctuating course and acute onset. The etiologies of delirium are multifactorial and diverse and often reflect the consequences of acute medical conditions， disease complications or drug intoxication. Delirium can have a variable presentation and need instruments to improve detection and diagnosis. Understanding the aetiology， assessment， and systematic detection and treatment programs appears beneficial for the elderly. We present the case of female 70 years old with altered mental status after her family noted a change in the patient's behaviour. For the past few days， the patient’s appetite waned， and she became agitated. Previously the patient had experienced diarrhoea for several days. After a comprehensive evaluation， the patient was diagnosed with hyperactive delirium due to electrolyte disturbances (hyponatremia and hypokalemia). Treatment is done by improving sodium and potassium levels and administering haloperidol. We discuss the presentation and management of this patient and review the treatment options of hyperactive delirium due to hyponatremia and hypokalemia.

【1】KEYWORDS delirium， treatment， hyponatremia， elderly

【2】Introduction

【3】In 2019， there were 703 million persons aged 65 years or over in the global population. The region of South-Eastern and Eastern Asia has the largest number of elderly (261 million). In In-donesia， the presentage of older adults in 2020 was 9，92% (26，82million). Bali is a province that has entered the old population structure phase (the percentage of the elderly population has been above 10 percent)， with the percentage of the elderly at11，58%(500 thousand)

【4】Delirium is a common neurocognitive disorder character-ized by acute changes in attention， cognition， and awareness， which experts describe as producing brain failure. The average incidence of delirium ranges from 29% to -64% in the elderly

【5】DuetoElectrolytelmbalanceinGeriatricPatients

【6】The term "delirium" was first used in the Diagnostic and Sta-tistical Manual of Mental Disorder (DSM) edition Ⅲ to describe acute brain dysfunction (formerly known as acute confusional state / ACS， acute brain failure， encephalopathy， ICU psychosis， or subacute befuddlement).

【7】Delirium is caused by various process disorders in the brain due to inflammation， aging， oxidative stress， neurotransmitter imbalances， endocrine disorders， and sleep disorders. These processes can be triggered by infection， metabolic disorders， electrolyte imbalance， anticholinergic drugs， psychoactive sub-stances，alcohol，etc.

【8】Electrolyte imbalances are commonly encountered in older patients because of a multitude of physiological changes and preexisting morbidities with the most common disorder in the elderly is hyponatremia.

【9】The elderly group (seniors) is a group that is prone to expe-riencing delirium. A history of structural brain or psychiatric disorders also increases the risk of delirium. However， delirium syndrome is often not diagnosed when the patient is at home or in a primary health facility， this is due to a lack of awareness of the symptoms of delirium， and often， the symptoms and signs that are shown are not typical. Whereas delirium is associ-ated with a longer hospitalization period， the incidence of com-plications， increased costs，long-term disability， and increased mortality regardless of confounding factors such as age， sex and comorbidities. So that appropriate management is needed for a better outcome

【10】The aim of this case report is to describe the proper manage-ment of delirium patients due to electrolyte imbalance and as a lesson to treat delirium patients in geriatrics to reduce mortality and morbidity due to delirium.

【11】Case report

【12】A 70-year-old woman was brought by her family to the emer-gency room with complaints of digressing of speech 2 days before being admitted to the hospital. Patients can not commu-nicate well， are rambling and sometimes stray from the subject and do not know the situation around the environment； other than that， the patient tends to be restless and babble to herself. This is the first time this incident has been experienced by a patient. Previously the patient was well conscious and able to communicate fluently. Before entering the hospital， daily activi-ties can be done without assistance. However， it was said that the patient's vision and hearing had begun to decrease a few years ago.

【13】Her family said that the patient previously had diarrhoea since 4 days ago， the stool had a liquid consistency， the color was yellow， there was no mucus or blood， a frequency of 8-10 times a day with an amount of about 20cc per bowel movement. Vom-iting is present but not profuse， containing only water and there was decrease of appetite. She has fever since 4 days， improved by taking paracetamol. Cough and shortness of breath is denied， urinate said no complaints. The patient does not take regular medication. The patient was said to have been diagnosed with diabetes mellitus since 5 years ago， but never took medication. Physical examination of the patient revealed delirium conscious-ness with the impression of moderate pain， VAS 0/10， blood pressure 130/80 mmHg， pulse 90 times per minute， respiration20 times per minute， and axillary temperature 38.6℃， with oxy-gen saturation of 99%. Anthropometric examination weight 45kg， height 162 cm and BMI 17.1kg / m2. On eye physical exami-nation， there was no anemic conjunctiva， physical examination of the thorax and abdomen did not reveal any abnormalities， on examination of the extremity， there was no edema， pain and weakness.

【14】From laboratory examination， it was found WBC 14.41，HB13.72， PLT 392.80， there was no worsening liver function SGOT67.4， SGPT 29.00， no worsening kidney function BUN 18.7， serum creatinine 0.86. On electrolyte examination， sodium lev-els were found to be 116， potassium 1.37. Examination of blood sugar at 223 mg / dl with an osmolarity of 251 mOsm/ kg. In the blood gas analysis， the results of metabolic alkalosis were obtained， with PH 7.67， PO2 128.00，PCO2 52.7， BE 35.6，HCO359.80， SO2 99%. Thyroid function tests and urinalysis were found within normal limits. Chest X-ray showed no abnormali-ties in cor and pulmo.

【15】Based on physical examination and laboratory result， this patient was diagnosed with hyperactive delirium ec electrolyte imbalance， hypoosmolar symptomatic hyponatremia， suspected dehydration， hypokalemia due to lack of nutrition and fluid loss(diarrhea)， acute gastroenteritis， suspected of bacterial differen-tial diagnose with viral infection， mild-moderate dehydration， diabetes mellitus type 2， with impairment of vision， hearing， total dependent disability and positive handicap. The therapy given to this patient was loading NaCl 0.9% 1000 cc followed by 30tpm， 75 meq KCl drip in 0.9% 20 tpm NaCl， ciprofloxacin200 mg every 12 hours iv， paracetamol 750 mg every 8 hours orally， insulin glargine 6 units every 24 hours， insulin aspart 4units every 8 hours， haloperidol 0.25 mg every 24 hours orally. After doing comprehensive geriatric care for 8 days， the patient’s condition gradually improved with awareness of composmentis and physical examination and laboratory result was improved.

【16】Discussion

【17】Delirium is a clinical syndrome characterized by impaired con-sciousness， cognitive function or perception that has a fluctu-ating and acute onset. Delirium diagnostic tools that are often used include using the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorder (DSM) criteria and the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM).

【18】The CAM algorithm is often used to diagnose delirium be-cause it has a sensitivity of 94-100% and a specificity of 90-95%， when used by a trained interviewer. In a meta-analysis per-formed on 1，071 patients， CAM had a sensitivity of 94% and a specificity of 89%. The performance of CAM can be reduced， if it is used by untrained interviewers. In this case， the diagnosis of delirium was confirmed by using the CAM criteria for the diagnosis of delirium， where a sudden change in consciousness was found， because the patient was previously able to communi-cate normally. Decrease of consciousness also fluctuates through-out the day， the patient is also unable to concentrate， where the patient sometimes talks to herself and wants to get out of bed and have a difficulties to follow the conversation. Her family also said that the patient speaks out of the topic. CAM criteria are often used in geriatric assessment， because these criteria have been validated so that they can be used for diagnosis. Most delir-ium presentations appear to be preceded by a prodrome phase， usually characterized by restlessness， sleep disturbances， irri-tability， and anxiety which usually develop over several hours to several days. The three classic motor presentations include hyperactive， hypoactive， and mixed type delirium Symptoms that appear in hyperactive delirium are agitation， psychosis， mood lability， refusal to take medical therapy， and other dyspruptive actions. Patients with the hyperactive type need supervision because the patient may unplug the ⅣV tube or catheter， or get out of bed and go outside. Meanwhile， hy-poactive type delirium is a form of delirium that actually occurs frequently but is rarely diagnosed. Patients with the hypoactive type appear confused， lethargic and lazy.

【19】In cases， the patient is often restless and the her speech is incoherent，the patient also tends to want to remove the IV and get out of bed， so that the patient is included in the hyperactive type delirium.

【20】The predisposing factors for delirium in this patient were 70years of age， the presence of visual and hearing problems and comorbid diseases， diabetes mellitus. Then delirium is triggered due to infection and electrolyte imbalance. Electrolyte imbalance that occur in patients include hyponatremia and hypokalemia.

【21】In this case， the patient has hyponatremia， where the inci-dence of hyponatremia in the elderly can be caused by many fac-tors， such as impaired water excretory capacity related to aging， as well as exposure to certain drugs and certain medical condi-tions. In this case， the patient has hypotonic hyponatremia， which is a condition where the loss of fluid is accompanied by loss of sodium， this condition is probably due to the patient’s diarrhea， besides that comorbid conditions such as diabetes mel-litus can also cause hypotonic hyponatremia. The prevalence of DM is quite high in the elderly population. Uncontrolled DM can cause osmotic diuresis and hypovolemic hyponatremia. In this uncontrolled DM condition， hypovolemia is an almost invariable finding due to osmotic diuresis and fluid loss accom-panied by electrolyte loss， which when accompanied by large water intake (without solutes) or administration of a more hypo-tonic solution can cause hypotonic hyponatremia. It should be noted， DM itself is associated with hyponatremia， regardless of the presence of hyperglycemia.

【23】Hyponatremia and several pathological conditions of the central nervous system are associated with swelling of the as-trocytes. Among all types of brain cells， swelling is mainly seen in astrocytes， especially in the astrocytic processes around the blood vessels. It is thought that the increase in astroglial cell volume is associated with a high water permeability of plasma and a high tendency of astrocytes to accumulate ions and neurotransmitters. The release of L-glutamate activated by cell inflammation causes hyperexcitability and mediates many of the other neurological manifestations of hyponatremia. Glutamate is known as the main excitatory neurotransmitter and is one of the organic osmolites that is extruded into the extracellular space during cellular adaptation to hyponatremia. Under hypoosmolar conditions， the extracellular glutamate con-centration of the brain increases.  A number of agents known to modulate glutamatergic neurotransmission have shown ef fectiveness in managing some forms of delirium， particularly the hyperactive and mixed types， such as valproic acid. Other antiepileptic agents with similar effects in GLU transmission also have a beneficial effect in managing hyperactive and mixed type delirium.

【24】In this case， the patient also has hypokalemia. Cerebral symp-toms in hypokalemia are uncommon. Symptoms of lethargy， apathy， drowsiness， confusion， irritability， delirium， and coma in hypokalemia are rare. They suggest that a related acid-base disorder or other electrolyte disorder may be responsible for this encephalopathy symptom.

【25】Conditions such as fever， hypotension， hypoxemia， hyper-glycemia， electrolyte disturbances， and acid-base imbalance can lead to increased intracranial pressure， decreased cerebral per-fusion pressure， and persistent cerebral hypoperfusion causing irreversible pathological lesions in brain tissue. Thelesions will become irreversible after cerebral blood flow， and cerebral perfu-sion have decreased for 6-8 hours. If the increase in intracranial force fails to decrease， perfusion to the brain will continue to decrease， and then the whole brain will become ischemic and deprived of oxygen. Lack of ATP decreases cell membrane XCeSS pumping function， excess calcium， and cell swelling or death. This is the final stage of neuronal death. As the pathogenetic factors and pathological mechanisms of brain damage gradu-ally become clearer， prevention and treatment will inevitably be increased.

【26】Delirium management

【27】Well-integrated care by doctors， nurses， other service providers， and even family members helps prevent the complications and bad outcomes often seen in delirium. Identifying and evalu-ating all modifiable contributors in delirium is essential， and a few small interventions can yield large benefits. The non-pharmacological approach is the first line to treat delirium symp-toms. The intake of fluids and nutrition must be considered because the patient is at risk of experiencing dehydration or malnutrition. Pharmacological treatment can be given if the pa-tient has the potential to harm himself or others， interfere with primary therapy， or develop symptoms of psychosis.

【28】Evaluation can be done through anamnesis and physical examination， including suggestions from elderly nurses and family members and laboratory examinations. Laboratory tests are specific to each patient， depending on clinical conditions (complete blood count， blood gas analysis， ammonia， sodium， calcium， thyroid function， cardiac evaluation). For example， a head CT scan is not routinely indicated in all patients with delirium， which is indicated in patients with head injuries， falls， history of anticoagulants， focal neurological signs or evidence of increased intracranial pressure. In this case， a head CT scan was not performed because there was no history of falls and neurological deficits.

【29】The triggering factor for delirium， in this case， is an electrolyte imbalance， such as hyponatremia and hypokalemia， which re-quires immediate treatment to prevent the development of delir-ium. Although there is no clear evidence that recovery of hy-ponatremia is associated with better outcomes， correcting for low sodium even in asymptomatic elderly is still recommended because it is associated with mortality and morbidity (e.g.， gait disturbances， falls， impaired cognition). The indication for treatment is stronger if the decrease in sodium levels causes symptomatic symptoms. In acute hyponatremia， hypertonic saline solution (3%) is usually used to acutely increase serum sodium levels and prevent severe neurological symptoms (e.g. seizures).

【30】If hyponatremia lasts more than 48 hours to develop or if the duration is unknown，correction should be made with caution. There is controversy about whether the degree of correction or the magnitude of hyponatraemia correction predisposes to neurological complications. It is difficult to separate the two variables because rapid corrections are usually accompanied by a larger amount of absolute correction over a period of time. The following three important principles can be applied in the correction of chronic hyponatremia：

【31】1\. Since the cerebral fluid is increased by about 10% in severe chronic hyponatremia， the goal is to increase the serum Na +level by 10%， or about 10 mmol /1 in the first 24 hours.

【32】2\. The correction speed shall not be more than 1.0 to 1.5 mmol/l at any given hour.

【33】3\. The goal of treatment is an increase of 6 to 10 mmol /1/24hours， but not more than 12 mmol /1/ 24 hours and 18 mmol/1/ 48 hours.

【34】In hypokalemia conditions， oral or enteral potassium is preferable if the patient can take oral medications and has a nor-mal gastrointestinal function. Acute hyperkalemia very rarely occurs when potassium is given orally. This reflects several fac-tors， especially the intestinal sensor， which minimizes changes in serum potassium levels. If potassium is given intravenously， acute hyperkalemia can occur if the speed of administration is too fast and can cause sudden cardiac death. Intravenous re-placement can generally be administered safely at a rate of 10mmol KCl / hour. If faster replacement is required， 20 or 40mmol/hr can be given via a central venous catheter， but continu-ous ECG monitoring should be used in these circumstances. In addition， there is an infectious condition in the patient that can cause delirium. In that case， the patient has been given empiric antibiotics for infection management.

【35】Nonpharmacologic strategies

【36】The delirium therapy strategy involves a team approach with active management of delirium risk factors using non-pharmacological interventions. Based on data on the prevalence of functional disorders and sleep cycle disorders associated with hospitalization， therapeutic strategies include efforts to improve social interaction and physical activity and optimize sleep cy-cles. The hospital environment can cause disruption of daily life and sleep cycles. So that effort are needed to minimize the negative effects of the hospital environment. The sleep cycle can be improved by optimizing lighting during the day， avoiding too bright light at night， and a thorough evaluation of the advan-tages and disadvantages of iatrogenic action during sleep (e.g. checking vital signs during sleep periods， frequent medication schedules etc.， which can interfere with sleep quality). Delirium non-pharmacological therapeutic strategy focused on psychomo-tor activity. Hypoactive delirium is dominated by somnolence， and these patients can be given stimulation therapy (e.g. con-stant interaction with family and caregivers， increased mobility， allowing direct sun exposure， and avoiding sleep in the morn-ing). In contrast， hyperactive delirium is dominated by agitation. These patients can be given de-stimulation therapy (eliminat-ing music， dimming the lights， eliminating confrontation， and rescheduling non-emergency laboratory sampling).

【37】Pharmacologic strategies

【38】The use of pharmacotherapy in individual delirium patients targets treatment at the underlying cause. Pharmacotherapy can also be used in cases where non-pharmacological interventions have failed. Medicines are usually prescribed when individuals suffering from delirium display agitation， hallucinations， aggres-sion， and paranoia that put them and their caregivers at risk of harm. The therapy given can be in the form of antipsychotics， benzodiazepines，cholinesterase inhibitor drugs， melatonin and melatonin inhibitors.
