【15】The colon of the prolapsed stoma was mostly viable but showed some partial necrotic change. During exploration of the ab-dominal cavity， a reddish small bowel loop 15 cm in length was found on the oral side 90 cm from the Bauhin valve， and it was determined that resection of this small bowel loop was unnecessary . Thus， 20 cm of the remaining sig-moid colon including the prolapsed colostomy with necrotic change was resected， and a new end colostomy was recon-structed at the preoperative stoma site in the right lower ab-dominal quadrant.

【16】The patient made an uneventful recovery and was discharged9 days after surgery. He is still alive with no stoma complica-tions or recurrence of rectal cancer 2 years after the surgery.

【17】Discussion

【18】Roughly 150 000 stomas are created in the United States an-nually . Unfortunately， the rate of stoma-related complica-tions ranges from 20% to 70%， and these complications can be grouped into early and late-occurring complications. Stoma prolapse is a late complication， and full-thickness protrusion of bowel through a stoma occurs in 2% to 26% of colostomies  and in some ileostomies and urostomies. Prolapse is more frequent with loop colostomies than with end colostomies at a ratio of approximately 3： 1 ， and it frequently involves the distal limb of the loop. Risk factors for stoma prolapse include patient factors such as advanced age， obesity， bowel obstruc-tion at the time of stoma creation， and lack of preoperative site marking by the enterostomal nurse . Techniques pro-posed to prevent stoma prolapse include extraperitoneal tun-neling， mesentery-abdominal wall fixation， resection of redun-dant colon， and limitation of the size of the aperture. In the present case， the sigmoid end colostomy was constructed in the right lower abdomen because the remaining sigmoid colon was elongated during a Hartmann operation. In fact， intraop-erative findings show redundant sigmoid colon， which seems to be the main cause of frequent stoma prolapse.

【19】Acute stoma prolapse can often be reduced at the bedside with the aid of sugar and ice to reduce bowel wall edema， thus allowing for an elective repair if the prolapse were to re-cur. Surgical options include new stoma reconstruction with resection of the redundant colon， and various methods were reported in the previous literature， such as Miwa-Gant muco-sal plication ， a technique similar to an Altemeier perineal proctectomy ， modified Delorme technique ， amputa-tion with a linear stapler ， and button-pexy fixation .

【20】Our patient suffered a prolapsed sigmoid end colostomy com-plicated by small bowel incarceration， which is very rare and has been reported in only 3 case reports  so far . Small bowel incarceration into a prolapsed colostomy is pre-sumed to occur if the small bowel becomes adherent to the prolapsed colon or accidental herniates into the potential space made by the colon intussusception associated with stoma pro-lapse. Operative findings from the 3 previous case reports in-dicated that they had all occurred by accidentally herniation， as in our case. However， our case is the first example in which small bowel incarceration could be reduced with manual com-pression before surgical treatment and the repositioned small bowel could be preserved. We decided to perform emergency surgery for the prolapsed colostomy because use of an anti-platelet drug had resulted in hemorrhage with uncontrollable oozing. The herniated condition and vascular insufficiency can be easily diagnosed with computed tomography. If we had prevented damage to and bleeding from edematous mucosa during gentle manual reduction， we might have been able to avoid emergency surgery.

【21】From this case， we suggest a treatment plan for prolapsed co-lostomy accompanied by small bowel incarceration . If a similar case is encountered， the surgeon should assess whether the patient has intestinal ischemia based on signs and symptoms， laboratory values and imaging studies. lf in-testinal ischemia is not suspected， preoperative manual re-duction for small bowel incarceration can be attempted. It is important to remember that surgeons should not hesitate to perform emergency surgery for uncontrollable hemorrhage or damage to the colostomy with compression as in our case. However， manual reduction with no complication may allow for elective surgery， including minimally invasive operation such as button-pexy fixation.

【22】Conclusions

【23】It is important to remember that small bowel can herniate into a stoma prolapse， and when encountering the acute presen-tation of a large stoma prolapse， careful manual reduction of the incarcerated small bowel may help to allow the selection of elective surgery instead of emergency surgery.

【0】Background：

【1】Case Report：

【2】Recent advances in the treatment of atypical hemolytic-uremic syndrome (aHUS) have resulted to better long-term survival rates for patients with this life-threatening disease. However， many questions remain such as whether or not long-term treatment is necessary in some patients and what are the risks of prolonged therapy. Here， we discuss the case of a 37-year-old woman with CFH and CD46 genetic abnormalities who developed aHUS with severe renal failure. She was successfully treated with three doses of rituximab and a three month treatment with eculizumab. After eculizumab withdrawal， symptoms of thrombotic micro-angiopathy (TMA) recurred， therefore eculizumab treatment was restarted. The patient exhibited normal renal function and no symptoms of aHUS at one-year follow-up with further eculizumab treatment.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】This case highlights the clinical challenges of the diagnosis and management of patient with aHUS with com-plement-mediated TMA involvement. Attention was paid to the consequences of the treatment withdrawal. Exact information regarding genetic abnormalities and renal function associated with aHUS， as well as estima-tions of the relapse risk and monitoring of complement tests may provide insights into the efficacy of aHUS treatment， which will enable the prediction of therapeutic responses and testing of new treatment options. Improvements in our understanding of aHUS and its causes may facilitate the identification of patients in whom anti-complement therapies can be withdrawn without risk.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Complement C5a ·Hemolytic-Uremic Syndrome· Thrombotic Microangiopathies The term atypical hemolytic-uremic syndrome (aHUS) applies to a heterogeneous group of diseases， which have in common thrombotic micro-angiopathy (TMA) associated with some de gree of renal failure， and frequently progress to end-stage re-nal disease or death . Compared with typical HUS， aHUS(5-10% of the HUS cases) is associated with a poor progno-sis . Multiple underlying disease mechanisms are likely to be involved in aHUS. In some patients with aHUS， the prima-ry underlying pathology involves a complement abnormality such as genetic mutation or the presence of an autoantibody to a complement component. The degree to which comple-ment components are implicated in other forms of aHUS is currently unknown 

【6】The complement cascade is the basis of innate immunity， and its regulation involves a delicate balance between comple-ment activity (for pathogen surveillance)， and complement control (for the avoidance of host damage and disease) . All of the three complement pathways (classical， alternative， and lectin) converge on the C3 complement. Unlike the clas-sical and lectin pathways， activation of the alternative path-way does not require initiators， thus hydrolysis of C3 can oc-cur spontaneously . Regulators of this process include：CFH， complement factor l (CFI)， MPC (CD46)， complement fac-tor B (CFB)， and C3. Inherited and acquired genetic mutations which affect these proteins are found in 60-70% of patients with the diagnoses of aHUS ，which recently has been de-scribed as complement-mediated TMA . These mutations lead to continuous activation of the alternative complement pathway. This over-activation results in endovascular cell in-jury and damage to the host tissues， which is very character-istic in TMA-disorders .

【7】Common variants in the genes encoding for CFH， CD46， and CFH-related proteins are known to be additional risk factor for the development of aHUS. Indeed， CFH mutations are the most common genetic abnormalities in aHUS (accounting for 25% of cases) and they are associated with poor prognosis regarding recurrence rates and development of chronic renal disease9. However， several studies have shown that only a CD46 aHUS-risk haplotype is associated with disease in patients that al-ready present with other mutations .

【8】Cases of aHUS may be sporadic or familial. Familial aHUS may display either autosomal dominant or autosomal reces-sive forms of inheritance. Environmenta. triggers， such as in-fections，medications， pregnancy， and systemic diseases have been reported to be precipitating factors for aHUS .

【9】The penetrance of familial aHUS is only approximately60% because the coexistence of a trigger and mutations (rare) or aHUS-risk haplotypes (common) in the complement genes is necessary for the manifestation of the disease . If the patients clinical history does not suggest any of the dis-eases associated with TMA， then the diagnosis of complement-mediate TMA should be made by exclusion and appropriate treatment should be initiated .

【10】Plasma exchange and plasma transfusion have traditional-ly been the first-line therapies for TMA . However， the finding that complement deregulation is fundamental to the disease has led to the implementation of targeted thera-pies， such as eculizumab， a monoclonal antibody that blocks the activation of the terminal complement pathway . Eculizumab has been reported to be effective in controlling hemolysis， improving renal function， and promoting the with-drawal of plasma therapy . Prior to the availability of an-ti-complement therapy， the 5-year risk for end-stage renal disease (ESRD) associated with aHUS was high (50-80%) and was related to the underlying genetic abnormality .Anti-complement therapy has improved the long-term health and quality of life of both children and adults with complement-mediated TMA .

【11】However， experience with eculizumab today is still limited. Many questions in relation to the treatment duration remain unanswered . The current treatment process is that C5blockade should be maintained in aHUS patients to prevent relapses and reactivation of the renal TMA process. However the risk of treatment-related adverse events and the high cost of the therapy， dictate a necessity for studies with the aim to investigate further the results of treatment withdrawal and alternative therapeutic options.

【12】We describe the case of a woman with CFH and CD46 genetic abnormalities who developed aHUS with severe renal impair-ment. Short-term treatment with eculizumab and rituximab was initially successful. However， TMA recurred after the with-drawal of eculizumab. She was once again successfully treat-ed when eculizumab was reintroduced for the duration of one year. We also reviewed the existing literature regarding ecu-lizumab withdrawal in aHUS. For the review， we searched by using the terms "atypical hemolytic-uremic syndrome"，“eculi-zumab withdrawal"，“complement-mediated TMA” in PubMed.

【13】Case Report

【14】A 37-year-old female smoker with no remarkable family history was admitted to our hospital after she had experienced mal-aise，weakness， nausea， loss of appetite， and abdominal pain for four days.Otherwise， she was asymptomatic and denied be-ing on any regular or new treatments. She had previously suf-fered three episodes of severe anemia and thrombocytopenia without renal involvement at the ages of two， five and 18 years. All of these episodes had been treated with plasma exchange and resolved completely.

【15】On admission to the hospital， the results of respiratory， cardi ac， and abdominal examinations were normal， except for the presence of peripheral edema. The patient was normotensive， eupneic，and afebrile. Before admission， the patient reported that her urine output was normal. Initial laboratory tests re-sults indicating TMA were： a low hemoglobin level (6.3 g/dL)， low platelet count (121×10 /pL)， high serum lactate dehydro-genase (1.916 U/L)， and the presence of schistocytes in a pe-ripheral blood smear. Haptoglobin was undetectable and direct Coombs test was negative. Results also revealed severe acute renal failure， with serum creatinine of 11.5 mg/dL， serum so-dium 132 mmol/L and serum potassium 6 mmol/L， mild pro-teinuria (urine analysis by dipstick gave a result of 3+，equiv-alent to 2-5 g/24 hour). Urine sedimentation showed 10-15red cells per high-power field (hpf) and 5-10 leukocytes per hpf. A renal ultrasonography was normal and a computed to-mography (CT) scan revealed mild bilateral pleural effusion. ADAMTS13 activity was normal and direct Coombs test was negative， so diagnosis of thrombotic thrombocytopenic pur-pura (TTP) and immune-mediated hemolytic anemia were eliminated. The patient denied any digestive symptoms (no diarrhea) and all microbiology studies were negatives (stool culture for STEC which would be indicative of Shiga-toxin HUS； HIV serology， influenza assay， and blood or pulmonary cultures). In view of these results， a preliminary diagnosis of aHUS was made. We therefore decided to start plasmapher-esis. Complete immunology studies (which were normal) and complement test were conducted prior to plasmapheresis ini-tiation. The patient was treated with five sessions of plasma-pheresis， steroids at a dose of 1.5 mg/kg per day and 48 hours of continuous hemofiltration followed by 14 daily sessions of hemodialysis without any response. A percutaneous renal bi-opsy was performed and the results demonstrated the pres-ence of TMA with diffuse glomerular damage and multiple in-tracapillary thrombi. Acute and chronic inflammatory cells had infiltrated the glomeruli and interstitium. Irregular glomerular basement-membrane thickening secondary to focal endotheli-al-cell proliferation was prominent. The small arteries and ar-terioles exhibited severe intimal hyperplasia and focal intralu-minal thrombi. Intratubular hyaline casts were also observed. On the basis of the accumulated results， a no complement-mediated aHUS was excluded.

【16】Treatment with eculizumab was initiated following previous vaccination against meningitis B， and 14-day prophylactic treatment of intravenous levofloxacin. Eculizumab was admin-istered following an induction schedule at a dose of 900 mg lV per week for four weeks， 1，200 mg on the fifth week， fol-lowed by a maintenance phase with a dose of 1，200 mg every two weeks. Plasmapheresis was discontinued before the first dose of eculizumab and steroids were progressively tapered(less 10 mg/day every week). Following the two initial doses of eculizumab neither the renal function nor the hemolysis pa-rameters improved， so plasmapheresis was resumed in com-bination with corticosteroids (1 mg/kg per day). Moreover， the patient received a dose of rituximab (375 mg/m²) per week for three weeks . After a total of four doses of ec-ulizumab and three doses of rituximab， renal function im-proved， therefore， the hemodialysis sessions were stopped. Six weeks following admission， the patient was discharged in good health， and the laboratory studies revealed progressive amelioration of renal dysfunction and hematological abnormal-ities with serum creatinine of 4.0 mg/dL. The patient report-ed no adverse effects from any of the treatments. Eculizumab was maintained throughout 12 more doses. During follow-up， creatinine and anemia continued to improve slowly but pro-gressively (creatinine nadir of 2.5 mg/dl). At that time， eculi-zumab was discontinued followed by close monitoring of the patient. After three months of the anti-complement therapy discontinuation， the creatinine level was 3.2 mg/dL and ab-normal hemolysis parameters were highly suggestive of TMA recurrence . Besides， genetic testing revealed， that the levels of complement factor H (CFH) and membrane co-factor protein (MCP， encoded by CD46) were below normal ranges. A mutation in the CD46 gene (c.390-1G>C) was de-tected， which is associated with increased risk of aHUS. The CD46 mutation was also present in the patient’s mother and brother. Moreover， the patient was homozygous for a poly-morphic variant CFH haplotype that also increases the risk of aHUS. On the basis of these results， eculizumab treatment at dose of 900 mg followed by maintenance at a dose of 1，200mg every two weeks was started again. Two weeks later， re-nal function and hemoglobin and platelet levels had returned to normal. After one year of further treatment with eculizum-ab， the patient's renal function remained almost normal with a creatinine level of 1.4 mg/dL and she exhibited no signs or symptoms of aHUS .

【17】Discussion

【18】We present a case of a patient with a very aggressive comple-ment-mediated aHUS and rapid early recurrence after with-drawal of eculizumab， which was successfully resolved after restarting eculizumab.

【19】The optimal duration of aHUS treatment and the correlations between genetic abnormalities and prognosis are not yet known. Historically， clinicians prefer to discontinue the plas-ma therapy for aHUS as soon as the patient is in remission， and treatment cessation has been included in the official rec-ommendation for the management of this disease . By contrast， individuals with genetic defects in the complement system are frequently plasma treatment-dependent and re-quire long-term weekly or biweekly plasma therapy to main-tain remission . Similarly， early cessation of eculizumab treatment is associated with a recurrence of aHUS probably because eculizumab is a terminal cascade blocking agent， and C3 convertase initially remains active in the glo-merular vasculature . A sustained course of treatment could be optimal to maintain the inhibition of complement activity. However， the very high cost of eculizumab and the unknown long-term effects of this treatment suggest that when decid-ing the optimal duration of treatment multiple variables should be considered 

【20】Several investigators have attempted to design individual-ized therapeutic schedules including the use of eculizum-ab and withdrawal protocols to avoid the risk of irreversible aHUS relapse 22-27.

【21】The monitoring of the complement-pathway activity tests might provide insight into the efficacy of aHUS treatment and enable the prediction of therapeutic responses and the implementa-tion of new treatment possibilities . A consensus has not early detection of relapse， which can be treated with the im-mediate re-initiation of complement blockade. Some investi-gators have discouraged the discontinuation of eculizumab therapy in patients with severe extra-renal manifestations  after kidney transplantation ， and when the glomeru-lar filtration rate is <20 mL/min/1.73 m² at the time of aHUS presentation .

【24】In some cases， eculizumab can be safely discontinued. Theoretically， in the case of antibody-mediated aHUS， the elimination of the antibody and the maintenance of immu-nosuppression therapy may be sufficient to control the syn-drome . An international consensual approach to the management of aHUS in children  recommended cessa-tion of eculizumab therapy when the anti-CFH antibody titre is <1，000 AU/mL Eculizumab cessation has also been recom-mended for antibody titres <2.5 times the upper limit of nor-mal . Immune suppression with cyclophosphamide or ritux-imab without anti-complement therapy has proved beneficial in antibody-mediated aHUS  Furthermore， withdrawal of eculizumab might be successful in individuals with isolated CD46 .

【25】In individuals in whom TMA has been controlled but renal func-tion has not recovered， eculizumab has occasionally been dis-continued， but this experience is currently too limited to justify a recommendation of continuous treatment with eculizum-ab for individuals on long-term dialysis routinely. A mutation in C5 that predicts a poor response to eculizumab has been described in a Japanese population. In individuals with aHUS who fail to respond to eculizumab， plasma exchange should be recommenced， and genetic analysis of C5 should be per-formed  .

【26】Taking into account the genetic results， the history of sev-eral episodes of TMA， and the aggressive relapse of the dis-ease， our patient was presumably at high risk for the devel-opment of ESRD and recurrence of aHUS， even though she presented with a CD46 mutation which is associated with a better prognosis than a mutation in CFH. We postulated that the aforementioned criteria could be a good reason to avoid discontinuation of eculizumab in these types of patients and long-term maintenance treatment with eculizumab could be beneficial and appropriate.

【27】Additional studies are required to provide more information on the utility of routine complement-pathway functional tests and other biomarkers， as well as genetic studies， to determine the eculizumab dosing schedules for individual patients. The current evidence does not support the cessation of eculizum-ab treatment in patients with CFH， CFB， CFI， or C3 mutations， whereas therapy could be stopped if close monitoring is per-formed in patients with mutations associated with better prog-nosis. However， our case report demonstrated that the with-drawal of eculizumab in patients with CD46 mutations is not always safe. An improved understanding of the interplay be-tween different genetic alterations and multi-organ patholo-gy in aHUS is required to determine which patients will ben-efit the most from a long-term anti-complement treatment.

【28】Conclusions

【29】This case highlights the clinical challenges of the diagnosis and management of patient with aHUS with complement-mediat-ed TMA involvement. Attention was paid to the consequenc-es of treatment withdrawal. Exact information regarding ge-netic abnormalities and renal function associated with aHUS， as well as estimation of the relapse risk and the monitoring of complement tests may provide insights into the efficacy of aHUS treatment， which will enable the prediction of ther-apeutic responses and the testing of new treatment options.

【0】ABSTRACTOromandibular limb hypogenesis syndrome (OLHS) is a rare congenital disorder with only a handful of cases reported worldwide. Likewise， isolated hypoglossia/macroglossia is rarer， with very few cases presenting for surgical procedures requiring anaesthesia. This case reports the successful anaesthesia management of a 5-year-old boy who presented for colostomy closure and had a previous history of difficult tracheal intubation.

【1】KEYWORDS hypoglossia， micrognathia， macroglossia， anaesthesia， case report

【2】Introduction

【3】Oromandibular limb hypogenesis syndrome (OLHS) is a rare spectrum of congenital disorders characterised by tongue， mandible， maxilla and limb malformations with an incidence of 1：175，000 live births. Around 50 cases of OLHS have been reported in English literature . Based on different character-istics， Hall classified it in 1971 for the ease of diagnosing them. Isolated hypoglossia， which is Type IA Hall’s clas-sification， is a rarer anomaly resulting in a "small rudimentary tongue." The tongue size is often a subjective assessment requir-ing careful examination， which explains the unknown incidence of isolated hypoglossia in newborns， with fewer than 30 cases reported worldwide . Most of these cases have presented with early airway compromise and feeding difficulties in the neonatal period or speech difficulties and dental problems later. How-ever， very few have presented for surgical procedures requiring anaesthesia J.

【4】Case Report

【5】A 5-year-old boy was weighing 17 kg presented to our institute for colostomy closure. The child was diagnosed with congenital anomalies at birth， like anal atresia and multiple craniofacial anomalies. The latter included low-set ears， malformed right ear， high-arched palate，hypoglossia， retrognathia and micrognathia. Computed tomography of the face and neck revealed mandibu-lar and maxillary hypoplasia， temporomandibular joint defor-mity， and decreased mastoid prominence with normal cervical vertebrae. The parents and the elder sibling of the child had no history of similar congenital disabilities. The mother had a posi-tive history of antenatal fever during the first trimester， for which she took intravenous ceftriaxone. The child had undergone surg eries such as sigmoid colostomy for anal atresia， mandibular distraction placement and removal， and posterior sagittal anorec-toplasty (PSARP). The anaesthesia records showed extremely difficult intubation during all these procedures， requiring elec-tive mechanical ventilation in the postoperative period.

【6】Examination revealed a moderately built child with normal developmental milestones. Airway examination revealed a re-duced mouth opening， a rudimentary tubular tongue， a nar-row mandibular arch， hypertrophy of the alveolar arches and impacted teeth . No palatal defects were observed. Echocardiography was normal， and a paediatrician evaluated the patient to rule out any systemic abnormalities.

【7】Combined spinal and epidural anaesthesia was planned due to a history of a difficult airway and the present airway exam-ination findings. The same was discussed with the operating surgeon， and consent was obtained from the child's parents. In the operating room， the patient was sedated with midazolam0.03 mg/kg，ketamine 1 mg/kg， fentanyl1 ug/kg and sevoflu-rane 2% to ensure immobility during regional anaesthesia. Even though mask ventilation was adequate， a proseallaryngeal mask airway (LMA) of appropriate size was inserted to avoid the sce-nario of airway obstruction and emergency establishment of a definitive airway in this patient. Meanwhile， a difficult air-way cart， including a fibreoptic bronchoscope and emergency tracheostomy， was prepared if needed.

【10】Image 1 Airway examination of the patient

【11】The patient was placed in a lateral decubitus position with knees to the chest. Under aseptic precautions， an epidural catheter was placed in L4-L5 interspace using a 19 gauge (G)5cm Tuohy needle and fixed at 6 cm at the skin. Subarachnoid block was administered in L5-S1 interspace using a 25GWhitacre needle， and 1.2 m1 of 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine with 50 ug of buprenorphine was given. The level of block achieved was T7. The intra-operative period was uneventful， and we could avoid postoperative elective mechanical ventilation with satisfactory analgesia using epidural top-ups.

【12】Discussion

【13】Environmental and genetic factors have been implicated in the aetiology of OLHS. Most of the reported cases are sporadic. A positive maternal history of drug intake or hyperthermia during the first trimester of pregnancy could result in a range of fetal defects . The present case had a positive prenatal history of maternal fever， which could explain the finding of isolated congenital hypoglossia.

【14】Direct laryngoscopy and intubation are extremely challeng-ing in these patients with an anticipated difficult airway. Fi-breoptic intubation is recommended as the first choice for gen-eral anaesthesia ， although patients with hypoglossia and high-arched palate allow proper placement of LMA as well. A1-ternatively， regional anaesthesia with sedation can effectively bypass the risks of managing such a challenging airway. In the present case， owing to the previous history of difficult intubation with the need for elective mechanical ventilation in the postop-erative period， we decided to administer combined spinal and epidural anaesthesia with sedation using LMA while maintain-ing spontaneous ventilation. Nevertheless， at the same time， a difficult airway cart was kept ready should LMA insertion get difficult， along with an inability to mask-ventilate the patient. Furthermore， systemic sedatives and opioids were administered in reduced doses to avoid the risk of postoperative complications like respiratory insufficiency and upper airway tract obstruction.

【15】Conclusion

【16】Isolated congenital macroglossia is challenging， especially from the anaesthetist's perspective. One should thoroughly under-stand airway abnormalities and alternate safer anaesthesia op-tions in these patients to plan immaculate anaesthesia， especially for elective surgeries.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Cholelithiasis in children was reported about three centuries back and remained relatively uncommon in the past， but now it is evolving and ever-increasing in frequency. We aimed to study the clinical presentation， predisposing factors， and treatment outcome of cholelithiasis in children in western Odisha. Methodology： The present prospective study was conducted on 38 patients less than 18 years old， with ultrasound proved cholelithiasis. Data were reviewed concerning patient demographic profile， clinical history， risk factors， imaging studies， operative techniques， postoperative complications， and treatment outcome. Results： 38 children (14 boys and 24 girls) with cholelithiasis were evaluated and treated during the study period and the mean age was 14.25±3.01 years (range 5 to 18 years). 44.73%of children (n=17) belonged to rural backgrounds， the rest to urban setups， and 23(60.52%) of patients belonged to the Hindu religion. In 63.15% of patients， no risk factor could be traced. 73.68% of children had multiple gallstones.28(73.68%) patients underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The average duration of hospital stay was 4.42 days. No major intraoperative or postoperative complications could be detected. Conclusions： In this region of the country， most children had no risk factors identified for cholelithiasis. The disease affected girls with middle socioeconomic status and urban areas belonging to the Hindu religion. In view of the high incidence of serious complications of gallstones in children and because of longer life expectancy we also recommend that expectant management of gallstones may not be safe and hence laparoscopic cholecystectomy must be done even in asymptomatic cholelithiasis.

【1】KEYWORDS Cholelithiasis， Childhood， Laparoscopic cholecystectomy， Outcome

【2】Introduction

【3】Gallstone disease is common in adults and represents a sig-nificant burden for health care worldwide. The prevalence of gallstones among the adult population in the worldwide vari-ability is 10% to 20% and in India is 3% to 6%1-3. Cholelithiasis is generally uncommon in children. But nowadays， the diag-nosis of gallstones in this age group is increasing due to the widespread use of ultrasonography (USG) in the diagnosis and management of every case of symptoms of pain abdomen or even in the evaluation of systemic problems like persistent fever， which led to increased detection of even asymptomatic gallblad-der calculi

【4】The exact prevalence of gallstones in children is not known.

【5】However， the probability of cholelithiasis in children should not be ignored. In 1959， the prevalence of cholelithiasis was noted0.15% among children till the age of 18 years’. Since that time， the prevalence has increased from 1.9% to 4.0% and the number of cholecystectomies in children increased accordingly8-10. In India， the only report by Ganesh et all has shown a prevalence of 0.3% in children11.

【6】Aim and Objectives

【7】There are very few studies in the Indian medical literature on cholelithiasis in children. The present study is aimed at giving some idea about the clinical presentation， predisposing factors， and treatment outcome of cholelithiasis in children of this region.

【8】Materials and Methods

【9】After permission was obtained from the Institutional Research Ethics Board(19242/Dt.30.11.19/IST-258/19)， this prospective clinical study was conducted in a tertiary care center in Odisha from oct-2019 to nov-2021.

【10】Inclusion criteria

【11】· Patients admitted with the diagnosis of cholelithiasis based on ultrasonography. Ultrasonographic diagnosis of cholelithiasis was based on the presence of echogenic foci that produced acoustic shadowing in the gallbladder or in the region of the gallbladder fossa.

【12】·Both male and female less than 18 years of age.

【13】Exclusion criteria

【14】·Patients were not willing to participate in the study.

【15】·Age more than 18yrs.

【16】Sample size

【17】A total of 38 cases of children (<18 years) with the diagnosis of cholelithiasis based on ultrasonography， who were admitted during the study period were included.

【18】Procedure

【19】The informed and written consent was taken from parents/guardians for participation in this study and all the participants were assured that the information provided was kept confiden-tial. A pre-designed proforma was used to gather information on the subject of study.

【20】Patients were evaluated on the basis of detailed history， thor-ough clinical examination， and relevant investigations. Patients were divided into two groups based on their symptomatology at the time of their initial diagnosis. The symptomatic group comprised those with typical features of cholelithiasis such as right upper quadrant abdominal pain， epigastric pain， nausea， vomiting， fat intolerance， and cholestatic jaundice and those with atypical features of nonspecific abdominal pain in areas other than right upper quadrant or epigastrium. The asymp-tomatic group comprised those children in whom cholelithiasis was diagnosed incidentally without any typical symptoms as described above.

【21】History of any hemolytic disorder， hepatobiliary disease， ab-dominal surgery， pregnancy， obesity， or bariatric surgery was noted. Exercise， drug history， diet， any past history of jaundice as well as menstrual history was recorded.

【22】A detailed general physical examination and systemic exami-nation were done. All routine baseline investigations were done which included CBC， KFT， Electrolytes， LFT， Routine urine ex-amination， Chest X-ray， X-ray abdomen， and ECG. All patients entitled to the study were subjected to ultrasonography of the abdomen and pelvis.

【23】The patients with symptoms were initially subjected to treat-ment with nothing per oral， IV fluids， antibiotics， and anti-spasmodics. Those who did not respond to conservative treat-ment were subjected to emergency cholecystectomy. Other pa-tients were treated with elective cholecystectomy. Cholecys-tectomy was also recommended for asymptomatic gallstones with chronic hemolytic anemia and asymptomatic large-sized gallstones (> 2 cm) for the risk of gallbladder carcinoma. Con-servative management with periodic clinical and sonographic assessment was done for asymptomatic children.

【24】The gallstones and gallbladder removed at the surgery were sent for chemical analysis and histopathological examination(HPE). After discharge from the hospital patients were followed up over the phone with queries focusing on persistence or resolu-tion of symptoms. Regular follow-up of these patients was done two weekly for a period of two months and afterward monthly for a period of four months to determine any subsequent com-plication or the resolution/recurrence of the symptoms.

【25】Data on age at diagnosis， gender， BMI， religion， settlement， socioeconomic status， clinical presentation (symptoms and du-ration of symptoms)， predisposing factors， ultrasonographic findings， biochemical and hematological investigations， asso-ciated comorbidities and its implications， mode of treatment， the surgical procedure adopted， type of stones， HPE findings， postoperative complications and length of hospital stay was recorded for each patient.

【26】The observations of the study are recorded in database pro-grammer SPSS version 21. Results on continuous measurements were presented as mean±SD and results on categorical measure-ments were presented in numbers (%). Microsoft Word and Excel 2016 were used to generate graphs， tables， etc.

【27】Results

【28】The present prospective series consists of 38 patients aged below18 years of age. The majority of the children were in the age group of 11-18 years which consisted of a combined 89.46%. The mean age group was 14.25 +/-3.01. The incidence of cholelithia-sis was more in females (63.15%)， from the urban areas (55.26%)， Hindus (60.52%)， and middle-class families (60.52%). The pre-disposing factors were identifiable in only 40% of children out of which hemolytic disease in 23.68% and obesity in 13.15%.Symp-toms were seen in 78.94% of children， out of which right upper quadrant pain was the most common symptom (42.10%) and21.05% of children were asymptomatic. The majority of children(56.66%) had symptoms for more than 1 week to 1 month. Ane-mia was noticed predominantly in 16 children (42.10%).73.68%of children had multiple stones and thickened GB wall was seen in 5.26%. Most of the children (76.36%) had a normal BMI.34 children (89.47%) underwent surgical management and 4(10.52%) children were managed conservatively. Out of 34 pa-tients， 28 (82%) underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy，and6(18%) open cholecystectomy. In 17 (50%) children had choles-terol stones. Out of 34 children who underwent surgery， 5 devel-oped mild postoperative complications (wound infection， serous discharge， and postoperative pyrexia). The HPE finding of the cholecystectomy specimens shows chronic cholecystitis in 20children (58.82%). The majority of the patients had a hospital stay of 4-6 days (64.70%).

【29】Discussion

【30】It was not possible to determine the true incidence of gallstones in the paediatric age groups because only those children referred to the radiology department for evaluation were included.

【31】The present study consists of 38 children below 18 years of age with a mean age of 14.25±3.01 years. There were no children in the age group of 0-5 years， 4 (10.52%) children were5-10 years， 16 (42.10%) children were 11-14years， and 18(47.36%) children were 15-18 years. Thus the maximum number of cases(87.5%) were found in the age group of 11 -18 years. Similarly， the studies conducted by Mehta S et al.12 reported the mean age was 13.10+/- 0.91 years， and Reif S et al.3 reported the mean age was 12.2 years +/-6.2 years. Most studies reported that the mean age of diagnosis ranges from 5 to 10 years (early childhood).

【32】In the present study， the females are more (63.15%) compared to males (36.84%) with a ratio of 1.71：1. Previous studies reported the incidence of gallstones among boys and girls is almost equal， where the mean age of diagnosis ranges from 5 to 10 years (early childhood)5，8，13-16. However， a female predominance was noted above the age of 12 from the beginning of adolocence58. Some previous studies had also reported a female predominance12，17This corresponds with the time at which cholesterol saturation in bile increases partly due to the secondary effects of hormonal changes (estrogen) during puberty preceding the development of cholesterol-related gallstones. In this study， there is female predominance as the mean age group was 14.25+3.01. However， male predominance was found in Kumar R et a1.18 studies and Bhasin SK et a1.19

【33】The majority of the children were from the urban region(55.26%)， belonged to the Hindu religion (60%)， and had a middle-class socioeconomic status (60.52%) which is consistent with the findings of the study conducted by Bhasin SK et al. The increased incidence among Hindus may be due to the ma-jority of the population or due to their dietary habits， which are comprised of fats and protein from animal and vegetable sources， or they may seek prompt medical attention very early or be more health-conscious than other religions.

【34】At the time of diagnosis， 30 children (78.94%) were clini-cally symptomatic， and 8 (21.05%) children had no gallstone symptoms. This result was consistent with other studies where the prevalence of symptomatic cholelithiasis ranges from 50-80%5，12，16，17，20-22. Right upper quadrant pain was the most common symptom in 16 children (42.10%)， followed by those with right upper quadrant pain associated with vomiting in 4(10.52%). Nonspecific abdominal pain was noticed in 5 chil- dren (13.15%)， whereas epigastric pain was noticed in 3 (7.89%) children and 1 (2.63%) child each was noticed to have fat intol-erance and cholestatic jaundice. Similarly in their study， Gocke et al.15， Dooki MR et16， and Deepak J et a1.17 reported that ab-dominal pain was the most common symptom (67% and 81.5%， respectively).

【35】Aetiology was idiopathic in 63.15% of children， obesity in13.15%， and haemolytic disorders in 23.68% of the children. Della Corte C et al.14 reported that 52.5% of patients had no risk factors， 24% had a family history， 7.6% had haemolytic disorders， obesity in 6.7%， and antibiotic consumption in 5%. Similarly， in their study， Gocke et a1.15 observed no identifiable risk factors in 43.5% of children， whereas； 16.1% had familial history， 12.9% had haemolytic diseases， 8.1% were overweight， and 12% of children had a history of antibiotic intake. The inci-dence of idiopathic gallstones in other reported studies varies from 23-77%58，17-19. In the past， many studies reported that hemolytic disorder constitutes about 20 -50% of the aetiology of paediatric cholelithiasis.5，8，12，23. However， in recent years， studies have found that this proportion has decreased because the other risk factors have become more prevalent. In this study， among the common identifiable factors was the hemolytic disor-der due to sickle cell disease (23.68%). This high percentage may be explained by the high prevalence (52%) of sickle cell disease patients within 15 years of age in western Odisha， as reported by Kar BC et a1.24. Obesity was reported as a frequent risk factor in children by Fradin K et a1.25 and Koebnick C et a1.26 whereas in this study， most children were observed within normal weight， and only 13.15% were obese.

【36】Anaemia was noticed in 16 (42.10%) children. Elevated ala-nine aminotransferase was noted in 12 (31.57%)and 6(15.78%) patients with elevated alkaline phosphatase. GGT and bilirubin were found elevated in 4 (10.52%) children each.

【37】The management of gallstones depends on the patient's symptoms and age， and there is no consensus about the man-agement of asymptomatic gallstones in children. Since pediatric laparoscopic cholecystectomy was first performed in 1990， its safety for children has been demonstrated and has proved to be advantageous over open cholecystectomy in children due to its minimally invasive nature， less duration of hospital stay， faster return to activity， decreased overall cost， decreased pain，and cos-metically better scar23. In this study， 34 (89.47%) children under-went surgical management， i.e. cholecystectomy， and 4(10.52%) children were managed conservatively. Laparoscopic cholecys-tectomy was performed successfully in 28 children (73.68%)and converted to open cholecystectomy in 6 children (15.78%). The study by Kumar DJ et al."? reported that laparoscopic chole-cystectomy (48.3%) was done predominantly in patients who presented with acute symptoms， and a few patients underwent surgery during follow-up. In their study， Della Corte C et al.4reported that laparoscopic cholecystectomy was confirmed to be an efficacy and safe procedure in treating pediatric gallstones for the low rate of postoperative complications (3%) and post cholecystectomy syndrome (4.7%).

【38】In the present study， there was no evidence of common bile duct stones preoperatively in any of the patients. In addition， none of the patients had any evidence of residual ducal stones during the follow-up period. Hence， a routine intraoperative cholangiogram was not recommended for the children.

【39】In the present series， most of the patients have multiple stones in 28 (73.68%) children， followed by a single stone in 6 children(15.78%)， and sludge and thickened gallbladders were seen in 2 children (5%) each. Dooki MR et al. reported that 19 (29%) patients had solitary gallstones； in 47 patients (71%)， there were multiple gallstones. Moreover， 3% of the patients had stones simultaneously in the common bile duct (CBD) and 1.5% in the cystic duct16. On the other hand， Bhasin SK et al. reported in their study that multiple stones were seen in 46 patients (57.5%)，28 patients (35%)had single stones， and 06 patients had biliary sludge/cholesterol is associated with gallbladder polyps Chemical analysis of the removed gallstones revealed that17 (50%) children had cholesterol stones， 10 (29.5%) children had mixed stones， and 7 (20.5%) children had pigment stones. This is comparable to Holcomb et al.， who observed that most patients had cholesterol stones23. In their study， Bhasin SK et al. observed that 65% of children had mixed stones， 20% had pure pigment stones， and only 15% had pure cholesterol stones.

【46】In this study， out of 34 patients who underwent surgery， 5 de-veloped mild or less severe postoperative complications (wound infection， serous discharge， and postoperative pyrexia). On the other hand， Bhasin SK et al.， in their study， reported no ma-jor intraoperative complications， and only 4 (5%) patients had intraoperative gallbladder perforation and spillage of bile.

【47】The Histopathological examination of the cholecystectomy specimen was found to be chronic cholecystitis in 20 patients(58.82%)， acute cholecystitis in 10 patients (29.41%)， and choles-terol in 4 patients (11.76%). In the study by Della Corte C et al.4the histological analysis of the removed gallbladders showed structural alterations such as chronic cholecystitis， papillomato-sis， and adenoma in most cases； in only a few cases， the gallblad-der wall was normal.

【48】All the patients were discharged home with an average hospi-tal stay of 4.42 days postoperatively (3-10 days)， and the majority(64.70%) stayed for 4-6 days. This followed the hospital stay re-ported by Gowda DJ et al."， 4.1 days (range 3-6days) and Bhasin SK et a1.19 3.82 days (3-8 days). All the patients were on regular follow-ups， and no patients were reported with recurrence of symptoms or with retained stones.

【49】No patient had stones spontaneously resolved in the present study. Probably the reason is that the rate of disappearing stones spontaneously has been detected higher， especially in children under 1 year of age， than in the other age groups， and in this study， there were no patients under 1 year old.

【50】Limitations of this study include the small sample size and the short duration of follow-up in some patients. Moreover， as the study was conducted in a tertiary care unit， many uncom-plicated cases may be diagnosed and managed in other centers without referral to our institution.

【51】Conclusion

【52】This study concluded that cholelithiasis in children is increasing in frequency in this part of the country， with female predomi-nance， with the majority from middle-class socioeconomic sta-tus， Hindu religion， and most of unknown aetiology. In view of this， the study recommends that further community-based larger studies are needed to establish risk factors for childhood cholelithiasis and prevention thereof in this part of the country. Symptomatic presentation is common among the pediatric pop-ulation. Given the high incidence of serious complications of gallstones in children and because of longer life expectancy， this study recommends that expectant management of gallstones may not be safe. Hence， cholecystectomy must be done even in asymptomatic cholelithiasis. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is a safe and efficacious treatment for cholelithiasis in children. Conservative management is supported for asymptomatic cases.

【0】Background：

【1】Thoracoschisis is a very rare congenital birth defect defined by the herniation of intra-abdominal organs through a defect in the thoracic wall. Though often associated with other birth defects as a part of the "limb-body wall complex”deformities， thoracoschisis has very rarely been reported as an isolated finding.

【2】Case Report：

【3】Here we present the case of a 30-day-old term male infant with an isolated left thoracoschisis managed suc-cessfully by primary closure. The patient was monitored postnatally in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Maputo Central Hospital because of the presence of a herniated mass through a left chest wall defect be-low the left nipple. Computed tomography (CT) scans suggested the presence of a left diaphragmatic hernia， left rib agenesis， and herniation of an unidentifiable intra-abdominal organ through the anterior left chest wall. On day of life (DOL) 30， when global health outreach pediatric surgeons arrived at the hospital， the decision was made to operate on the child. The mass was found to be of liver origin， the exposed tissue was excised， and primary closure of the chest wall was accomplished. The patient's postoperative course involved a wound infection that resolved favorably with treatment， allowing for discharged home on postoperative day (POD) 17in stable condition.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Our case report highlights the importance of recognizing this rare condition and directing appropriate surgical care.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Congenital Abnormalities · Congenital， Hereditary， and Neonatal Diseases and Abnormalities· Hernia·Mass Chest X-Rav · Pediatrics Thoracoschisis is a rare congenital birth abnormality consist-ing of the herniation of intra-peritoneal organs through a de-fect in the thoracic wall. Thoracoschisis is classified as a part of the “Limb-Body Wall Complex” (LBWC) deformities， being more commonly associated with other birth defects such as limb agenesis， anterior thoracic wall deformities， phocomelia， and diaphragmatic hernias . However， of the 14 total re-ported cases of thoracoschisis， 5 cases had no other related abnormalities .

【7】The etiology behind thoracoschisis is still unidentified， but the presence of the other associated LBWC deformities gives insight into the timing at which these deformities likely develop . Initial theories behind the pathogenesis of LBWC deformities include abnormal embryonic folding， formation of amniotic bands that interfere with limb development， rupture of amni-otic sacs， and vascular malformations .

【8】Diagnosis of the full extent of the defect differs on a case-by-case basis， but usually involves chest radiography (CXR) or computed tomography (CT) scans . Exploratory opera-tions are often necessary as it is sometimes unclear whether there is an elevated hemidiaphragm or a diaphragmatic her-nia . Prenatal diagnosis of thoracoschisis has been suc-cessfully demonstrated using 2D and 3D ultrasound . Treatment of thoracoschisis is varied but involves primary management to assure hemodynamic and respiratory stability， followed by imaging for diagnosis， and finally either surgical reduction of abdominal contents through subcostal incision or gastroschisis-like silo bags. This is followed by closure of the thoracic wall， re-approximation of separated ribs， or plans to do staged reconstruction of the thoracic wall post-opera-tively . In this case report we present a rare instance of a term male infant with an isolated left-sided thoracoschi-sis and rib agenesis.

【9】Case Report

【10】During a one-week global health outreach to Maputo， Mozambique， a 30-day old male infant was identified in the NICU of Maputo Central Hospital， Mozambique with a 3x3 cm mass overlying the left chest wall located below the left nip-ple . The mass was nonreducible， contiguous with the surrounding skin， and covered by friable granulation tissue. Upon further examination of the chest wall， there was a large surrounding defect in the rib cage around the protrud-ing mass. There were no underlying palpable ribs at the loca-tion of the mass and no pectoral muscle present on the affect-ed side. In addition， there was an accessory nipple complex located inferior to the mass. The rest of the physical exami-nation was unremarkable.

【11】Upon review of the patient's medical records we discov-ered that the infant was born by means of vaginal delivery to an otherwise healthy 20-year-old female in Tete province， Mozambique. Of note， she had received no prenatal care and contracted malaria during the first trimester of pregnancy. Immediately after birth the child was stable， needing no ventilatory assistance. He was subsequently transferred to Maputo Central Hospital NICU for further management ofthe left chest wall mass. The patient was evaluated by an echo-cardiography， which was deemed normal， as well as CXR and a CT of his chest ， which delineated a possible left-sided diaphragmatic hernia， with multiple partial rib agene-sis surrounding the area of the chest wall herniation. It was unclear based on the CT images whether the herniated mass contained parts of the left liver or lung.

【12】The decision was made to take the child to the operating room(OR) for definitive repair. As the initial images were sugges-tive of an associated left diaphragmatic hernia， we approached the repair by left subcostal incision . It became im-mediately obvious that the diaphragm was very high in the left chest， but was intact and without a defect. Next， we tried to reduce the mass back into the abdominal cavity， but with-out success. Mobilization of the mass from the chest wall was accomplished by a combination of blunt and electrocautery dissection. Upon further inspection， we determined that the mass was originating from the left lobe of the liver. At this point， we decided to excise the exposed tissue at the level of the chest wall and allow the liver to retract back into the ab-domen. The chest wall was then closed in layers . Postoperative recovery was complicated by the presence of an infection at the wound site， which subsequently resolved with antibiotic treatment， allowing for discharge on POD 17.

【13】Discussion

【14】Thoracoschisis is a very rare congenital abnormality， hav-ing only been reported 14 other times in the medical litera-ture . In direct contrast to thoracoabdominoschisis， thoracoschisis is not a midline defect and does not involve the abdominal wall. Davies et al. first described it in 1977 as be-ing associated with chest wall malformations and diaphrag-matic hernias . Since then， other cases have been noted to be associated with limb abnormalities， being classified as a part of the group of defects known as "Limb-Body Wall Complex" (LBWC) deformities . Only 5 of the reported cases of thoracoschisis have had no other related defects， termed“isolated thoracoschisis". Our case falls into the category of isolated thoracoschisis.
