【26】In a comparative study where the outcomes of recipients of third and fourth kidney transplantation were compared with first and second transplantations， no significant difference was found in graft and patient survival over 5 years of follow-up. The 5-year allograft survival was 83.6% for the first transplan-tation， 85.6% for the second transplantation， and 95% in the third and fourth transplantation. The 5-year recipient survival was 82.5% for first， 100% for second， and 95% for third and fourth kidney transplantation. On comparing the living donor HLA incompatible versus the deceased donor compatible third and fourth transplantations， no statistical difference was seen in the allograft survival or estimated glomerular filtration rate at any time between the 2 groups . All the aforementioned studies are summarized in Table 1.

【27】Our patient who underwent a third kidney transplantation af-ter desensitization for simultaneous blood group and HLA in-compatibility had a good graft function at least in the short-term. Even with limited resources the results are at par with the developed world.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Insulinomas are a rare group of neuroendocrine tumours. Ninety percent are benign and most are solitary. They can have varied presentations and long-standing history of symptoms. Most patients are affected in the fourth to sixth decades of life. Insulinomas can have an association with multiple endocrine neoplasia(MEN) type 1. However， typically they are sporadic. Most are solitary and benign. Their most common presentation is symptomatic hypoglycemia. After investigations， surgery is the treatment of choice and can offer cure. Laparoscopic surgery can provide all the benefits of minimally invasive surgery and at least equal oncological outcomes in high volume centers. 3D laparoscopy can further improve outcomes with better depth perception and control during the surgery. Case Presentation： This case report is about an 80-year-old female who presented to us with long-standing symptoms of hypoglycemia. She was symptomatic for at least seven years before she was being diagnosed. Her symptoms gradually became severe in three months before she presented to us. After confirmation of the diagnosis with biochemical and radiological investigations， she was treated with 3-D laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. Histopathology was consistent with insulinoma， and she had resolution of symptoms. Conclusion：Insulinomas are rare neuroendocrine tumours. There shall be a high index of suspicion for these disorders. Management is multidisciplinary. Surgery is the treatment of choice. Proper management leads to rapid cure and resolution of the symptoms.

【1】KEYWORDS insulinoma， neuroendocrine， laparoscopy， 3-D laparoscopy Endoscopic ultrasound， multiple endocrine neoplasias

【2】Introduction

【3】Insulinomas are a rare group of neoplasms that arise from insulin-producing beta type islet cells . The annual incidence is around four cases per million individuals per year . Indi-viduals are mostly affected in the fourth to sixth decade of life with gender predilection for females . Up to 90% of these tumours are benign. They constitute the most common group of functional pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (pNETS). Ten percent of the insulinomas are multiple， around 10% are ma-lignant ， and 10% are having an association with syndromes such as Multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 1 (. Due to the indolent nature of the tumour and non-specific symptoms， the presentation is often delayed， and the patient attends various specialties before being finally diagnosed. There is a classic triad of low blood sugari.e. <55 mg/dl， hypoglycemic symptoms and improvement in the symptoms after the provision of glucose. This is referred to as Whipple's triad. Insulinoma can be sus-pected if there are symptoms of Whipple’s triad in the presence of Insulin levels > 3pU/mL and C-peptide levels >0.6 ng/mL. 72-hour fasting test is the gold standard for the diagnosis of insulinoma 71.

【4】After biochemical confirmation， the next goal is the localiza-tion of the tumour and exclusion of metastasis. Localization of insulinoma can be difficult. Starting from Ultrasound， CT scan and MRI are useful for the localization of the tumour. Endo-scopic ultrasound (EUS) is of paramount importance in local-ization of the tumour as well as to depict the relationship of the lesion with the pancreatic duct， nearby vasculature and the ability to further perform endoscopic ultrasound guided fine needle aspiration (EUS-FNA). EUS has detection rates of 86.6-92.3%. Other invasive procedures such as Angiography and arterial stimulation venous sampling (ASVS) can help to diagnose the location of the tumour by utilizing the endocrine function of the tumour， in cases where the initial studies fail to localize the lesion.

【5】Surgical excision is the treatment of choice. However， the choice of procedure depends on many factors such as the loca-tion of the tumour in the gland， proximity to the duct system and whether the lesion is single or multiple. For lesions that are either malignant， relatively large-sized， close to the ductal system and located in the head， pancreaticoduodenectomy is warranted. Smaller lesions in this region and away from the duc-tal system can be treated with enucleation. For lesions of body and tail similarly either distal pancreatectomy and enucleation can be carried out depending on above mentioned factors .

【6】The present case report is about our experience of manage-ment of an 80 year old patient of insulinoma who had long-standing symptoms that gradually worsened.

【7】Case presentation

【8】We report a case of an 80-year-old woman who presented to us with history of dizziness， sweating and altered sensorium for seven years. The symptoms gradually worsened over a period of previous three months. She also reported a few episodes of fall and getting unconscious. The condition of the patient used to improve after meals. Her blood sugar levels were found low during these episodes. The episodes were more frequent and profound by the time the patient sought medical attention at our center. Her medical history was significant for osteoarthritis and well-controlled hypertension. She had no previous surgical history. She was a mother to six.

【9】Upon presentation to the hospital she underwent routine hematological and biochemical investigations. She was drowsy and irritable. Her random blood sugar levels came out to be 39mg/dl. She was hospitalized and treated with glucose infusion. Her insulin and C-Peptide levels were obtained that came out to be 12 pU/mL and 9.21ng/ml. During the course of her admis-sion and investigations at the hospital， she became unconscious. Her blood glucose levels were again obtained. This time critical alert was received for blood sugar levels of 28 mg/dl. Thus， she was treated with continuous dextrose infusion. Her planned72-hour fasting test was cancelled due to her frail condition and ongoing severe symptoms of hypoglycemia. Clinically and on the basis of biochemical investigations the diagnosis of insuli-noma was almost certain. Thus， it was decided to proceed to localization investigations.

【10】She had a CT scan of Chest， Abdomen and Pelvis with con-trast that demonstrated a 20x 18 mm arterially enhanced lesion in the tail of the pancreas. It was a solitary lesion with well defined margins. CT scan findings favored a primary pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour without any distant metastasis. Endo-scopic ultrasound was performed. The lesion was assessed， it was found to be in close proximity of the pancreatic duct. More- over， the EUS complimented the findings of the CT scan. EUS-FNA was obtained and results favored a well differentiated neuroendocrine (NET) tumor.

【11】As she had ongoing symptoms and her symptoms were only managed by continuous dextrose infusions， she was planned for resection on emergency list. She was planned for 3-Dlaparo-scopic distal pancreatectomy on next available list. Meanwhile her assessments and work-up was performed urgently.

【12】The operating team consisted of operating surgeon， an assis-tant surgeon and a camera assistant. We used modified Lloyd Davis position. Four 5mm working ports and one 11mm camera port were utilized. We use LigasureTM (Mary land) dissector as energy device. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed no metastasis. After exposure the tumour was found in the tail of pancreas closely abutting the splenic hilum. The pancreas was transected with Echelon stapler after the splenic artery and vein were sepa-rately clipped using Hem-o-loks. Pancreatic remnant was over-sewen with prolene. Jackson Pratt (JP) drain was placed in the splenic bed. Operative time was 150 minutes. Intra-operative blood loss was 30 ml. The patient stayed in intensive care unit for one day and was stepped down to the floor the next day. Drain was removed on day three and she was discharged the same day in stable condition. She had smooth recovery other than a urinary tract infection that was medically managed.

【13】Histopathology came out as well-differentiated neuroen-docrine tumour World Health Organization (WHO) Grade I. Mitosis was reported less than2/2mm-.Ki-67 was 2% with pos-itive synaptophysin. Grossly it was 2.1 cm in greatest dimension and margins were free of tumor. There was islet cell hyperplasia seen that was consistent with nesidioblastosis， a phenomenon seen in insulinomas of pancreas. Her case was discussed in the hospital Multidisciplinary Tumour (MDT) board and no further oncological treatment was advised.

【14】Post-operatively， patient had normalization of the blood glu-cose levels. Later the blood glucose levels went in the diabetic range. Currently， the patient is eight months post-surgery and is free from symptoms. Her HbA1C currently is 7.1

【15】Discussion

【16】Insulinoma is a rare tumour and has an indolent course with the clinical signs and symptoms that can mimic other common medi- cal disorders. Most of the symptoms are related to hypoglycemia. Most common being confusion， changes in the behavior， visual disturbances， dizziness， seizures and loss of consciousness， anxi-ety， sweating， palpitations and tremors . These symptoms can also be present in a variety of other medical and psychiatric disorders. Thus it is common for these patients to present late and present to various specialties and get treated based on symp-toms before they land to either endocrinologists and surgeons. Commonly， there is a delay for more than 15 months before the disease is diagnosed . In our case， the patient had symp-toms for seven years before she was being diagnosed. The age group in which disease is common is fourth to a sixth decade ； however， our patient presented in the eighth decade of her life.

【17】Insulinoma can occur in conjunction with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN)-type-1 which includes parathyroid hyperpla-sia， anterior pituitary adenomas and pancreatic or duodenal neuroendocrine tumours. It is an autosomal dominant disorder. Insulinomas that occur in conjunction with this disorder are often multicentric and develop earlier in life as compared to the sporadic cases .

【18】The diagnosis and localization of the tumour is the trickiest part. One has to have a high index of suspicion for these lesions. The classic Whipple's triad， along with C- peptide and insulin levels play an imperative role in the diagnosis of the lesion . In our case， the patient had all the typical symptoms of Whipple’s triad and had raised C-peptide and insulin levels as well. The 72hour fasting test is considered gold standard for the diagnosis. However， our patient was old， frail and fairly symptomatic with repeated bouts of hypoglycemia with very low blood sugar levels； thus， it was not possible to carry out a 72-hour fasting test.

【19】After diagnosis， the next imperative step is localization of the tumour. Contrast-enhanced CT scan is thought to be the first-line investigation. Helical contrast-enhanced CT scan has a sensitivity of around 94% . EUS has become the modality of choice in the localization of these tumours. It can pinpoint the exact location， its relation to the pancreatic duct and biliary tree along with surrounding vasculature. Its sensitivity is around94-96%. However， the main issue with EUS is user dependabil-ity J. ASVS can be a useful modality in cases where the localization is still a problem . However， it is an invasive pro-cedure like EUS. It requires equipment and trained personnel to do it， hence not routinely done and available. At our institution， we routinely perform CT scan， MR and EUS for these tumours and other neuroendocrine tumours of the pancreas. Similarly， in this case -CT scan and EUS were used for the localization of the Surgery is the mainstay of the management of insulinoma， if adequately performed， the patient can be cured . The choice of procedure depends on the location of the tumour， whether its solitary or multiple， the relationship of biliary and pancreatic ducts and the presence of suspicious lymph nodes. Tumour enucleation is the procedure of choice if the tumour is solitary superficial and free of nearby ducts . Most of the lesions have a distinct appearance that can be recognized at the surgery； and there is a well-defined plane that can be used for enucleation. For cases that are in close proximity to the ductal system， major vasculature and there is suspicion of malignancy resection of the pancreas is a better option to avoid pancreatic fistulae and vascular complications. Surgical resection options include pancreaticoduodenectomy， distal pancreatectomy with or without splenectomy and central pancreatectomy. In our case， as the lesion appeared to be in close proximity to the pancreatic duct and was closely abutting the splenic hilum thus we opted for distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy.

【20】The laparoscopic approach is increasingly used and favoured approach for the management of pancreatic lesions in high vol-ume centers. It decreases the morbidity. Oncological outcomes are however similar. The use of laparoscopic ultrasound can fur-ther aid in the localization of the tumour Moreover， the 3-D approach gives better depth perception and further makes la-paroscopic surgery easy and productive . Our case was done by 3-D laparoscopic approach. At our institute， we routinely use3-D High Definition laparoscopy for hepatopancreatic-biliary(HPB) surgery as well as upper and lower Gastrointestinal surg-eries.

【21】Histologically these lesions are neuroendocrine in nature. They have a strong expression of chromogranin and synapto-physin. Ki-67 index and number of mitosis per high field are used to differentiate between grades of tumour. caseOur case was low grade neuroendocrine tumor on the basis of these cri-teria. The diagnosis of malignancy can be difficult to make and only becomes apparent once there are established metastasis.

【22】Conclusion

【23】Insulinomas are rare tumours. Most are benign. Physicians shall have a high index of suspicion based on the symptoms. Management is multidisciplinary and involves endocrinologists， physicians from various specialties， surgeons and pathologist. Insulinomas can be difficult to localize， and there are different investigations with varied accuracy； thus， judicious use shall be made， however， it is imperative to localize the lesion prior to surgery. Surgery， preferably laparoscopy， is the treatment of choice and offers a cure.

【0】Background：

【1】Laparoscopic cholecystectomy is a commonly performed surgical procedure. In certain situations visualiza-tion of the Callot triangle can become difficult due to inflammation， adhesions， and sclerosing of the anato-my. Without being able to obtain the “critical view of safety" (CVS)， there is increased risk of damage to vital structures. An alternative approach to the conventional conversion to an open cholecystectomy (0C) would be a laparoscopic subtotal cholecystectomy (LSC).

【2】Case Report： We present a case of a 56-year-old male patient with acute cholecystitis with a "difficult gallbladder” man-aged with LSC. Due to poor visualization of the Callot triangle due to adhesions， safe dissection was not feasi-ble. In an effort to avoid injury to the common bile duct (CBD)， dissection began at the dome of the gallblad-der allowing an alternative view while ensuring safety of critical structures.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】We discuss the potential benefits and risks of LSC versus conversion to OC Our discussion incorporates the pathophysiology that allows LSC in this particular circumstance to be successful， and the considerations a sur-geon faces in making a decision in management.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Cholecystectomy· Cholecystectomy， Laparoscopic · Gallstones · Laparoscopes Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is one of the most com-monly performed surgical procedures throughout the world. Ever since Langenbuch developed the technique for open cho lecystectomy (0C) over a century ago， it has become the gold standard for treatment of symptomatic cholelithiasis . In1985， Muhe performed the first LC . This was a major step in integrating advances in surgical techniques， as the benefits of laparoscopy were introduced to symptomatic cholelithiasis treatment. LC achieves shorter recovery time， decreased ex-pense， less postoperative pain， and improved cosmetics . There are certain situations where visualization of the Callot triangle becomes difficult due to inflammation，adhesions， and sclerosing of the anatomy. The inability to obtain the“critical view of safety"(CVS) and identify the cystic duct， cystic artery， and common bile duct (CBD) alters how the surgeon must pro-ceed . The standard of care has been to convert the proce-dure to an OC . Depending upon the patient’s comorbidi-ties and the surgeons comfort level， an alternative approach to conversion to an OC can be a laparoscopic subtotal chole-cystectomy (LSC).

【6】Case Report

【7】A 56-year-old male presented to our emergency department(ED) with epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant of one-week duration. The patient reported having prior ab-dominal symptoms that he believed were not severe enough to warrant a trip to the ED. Initial laboratory results indicated leukocytosis of 15.6. His physical examination findings were consistent with acute cholecystitis. He had a past medical his-tory of brain cancer with four courses of chemo-radiotherapy.

【8】Imaging studies were performed to support the diagnosis of cholecystitis. An abdominal ultrasound displayed multiple echogenic shadowing gallstones within the gallbladder， a dif-fusely thickened wall measuring 0.57 cm， and the CBD mea-sured 0.60 cm . No dilatation of the CBD was pres-ent； consistent with the patient's liver function tests being within the normal limits.

【9】The patient was scheduled for a LC with possible conversion to OC. Intraoperatively， adhesions were noted between the gall-bladder， omentum and duodenum . At that point， 20cc of bile were drained from the patient’s distended gallbladder.

【10】The gallbladder wall was noted to be friable. The infundib-ulum along with the ducts， including cystic duct and artery， were embedded in fibrotic adhesions making it difficult to ob-tain the CVS during dissection . Visualization of the Callot triangle was unobtainable， thus safe dissection was not feasible. With hemostasis maintained， the decision to remain laparoscopic and perform a LSC was made.

【11】We turned our attention to the lateral wall of the gallbladder， where an incision was made along the dome of the gallblad-der dissecting it from lateral to medial. The anterior， medial， and lateral wall of the gallbladder were removed with elec-trocautery down from the fundal dome until the infundibu-lum of the gallbladder was reached leaving the posterior wall intact with exposed mucosa. The intraluminal cystic duct was identified . The stones and excised gallbladder wall were removed . Irrigation and suction removed re-sidual bile from the infundibulum basin. Electrocautery was used to score the posterior wall mucosa. The visualized intra-luminal cystic duct was not itself cauterized to prevent dam-age to unidentified structures lying in close proximity， partic-ularly the CBD. A Jackson-Pratt (IP) drain was placed within the basin of the infundibulum connected to a suction bulb in order to monitor any bilious drainage through a patent cystic duct. The patient was discharged from the hospital one day postoperatively with the JP drain remaining in place.

【12】At one week postoperative， there was bilious drainage not-ed from the JP. At the second postoperative week， there was less than 5 mL serous fluid drained， and the JP drain was re-moved. The patient has reported no postoperative complica-tions since the procedure and no abdominal pain.

【13】Discussion

【14】Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is the “gold standard" pro-cedure for cholecystitis. In the event that a surgeon encounters a"difficult gallbladder，" laparoscopic subtotal cholecystecto-my (LSC) is a viable option. When presented with the scenar-io where delineation of the Callot triangle would be difficult and pose a hazard to proper identification of the anatomy， LSC versus conversion to OC should be considered.

【15】The introduction of open subtotal cholecystectomy by Madding in 1955 presented a safe alternative to a total cholecystecto-my by preventing misidentification of the cystic duct . Since then， LC has been converted to OC in cases of difficult dissec-tion and a prolonged surgery without progress. Early identifi-cation of the “difficult gallbladder" and the subsequent deci-sion to change the management course to a LSC prevents the need to perform two procedures， the attempted LC and sub-sequent open procedure， thus reducing operative time.

【16】In this particular case， the cystic duct was left patent and the mucosa was scored by electrocautery along the back wall and near the infundibulum. The proposed pathophysiology was that heat from the cautery causes subsequent sclerosis of the cystic duct. However， this must be done cautiously sincebile duct and nearby soft tissue can be sclerosed by exces-sive heat . It can be difficult to control the extent of scle-rosis， due to electrocautery causing damage or strictures to nearby structures. Unique to this case was the use of electro-cautery as opposed to the alternative options of intracorpo-real suture or an endoclip to secure the cystic duct. The re-sults of the procedure were monitored externally by measuring the decreasing JP drain output. If bilious drainage continued， then endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with stenting would be the subsequent next step， identifying anatomy， promoting drainage from the main pancreatic duct， and allowing for sclerosis of the cystic stump. In this particu-lar case， bilious drainage decreased without further interven-tion， as monitored externally via the JP drain.

【17】The risks of performing a LSC must be weighed against any potential benefits on a case-by-case basis. There is still a risk of bleeding since tissues are inflamed and friable. Additionally， bile leakage and difficulty removing spilled stones are more common when performing a LSC . In addition； the patient may develop continued biliary drainage necessitating ERCP with stenting .

【18】LSC has the short-term perioperative benefits of remaining laparoscopic. Long-term， there have been no cases reveal-ing cholecystitis， abscess formation， or cancer in the remnant gallbladder tissue according to Tamura et al. OC remains the ideal procedure for insuring hemostasis. The determina-tion of technique to use ultimately is determined by surgeon preference， as the goal of either technique is to avoid dam-age to the CBD. The definitive operation with removal of the entire gallbladder is always the preferred option，reducing the chance of retained stones and subsequent attacks， however， not at the expense of additional risk. Circumstances of each case contribute to the decision of how to proceed with a dif-ficult gallbladder.

【19】Upon visual inspection of the gallbladder intraoperatively， the decision of how to proceed must be made. When pre-sented with friable， dense adhesions that make obtaining the CVS difficult， a modified approach must be considered to avoid inadvertent damage to critical structures. The authors of this paper agreed that with select patients， LSC is a viable and preferred option. This procedure， in particular the use of electrocautery causing local sclerosis in proximity to the cys-tic duct， is an alternative option for management in LSC， that

【0】Background：

【1】Right atrial myxoma accounts for 15-20% of cardiac myxomas and syncope is a very rare manifestation. We present the case of an 89-year-old man with right atrial myxoma and syncope， and discuss the role of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in the diagnosis of myxomas.

【2】Case Report：

【3】An 89-year-old man with a history of hypertension， hyperlipidemia， chronic kidney disease stage 4， mild de-mentia， and benign prostatic hyperplasia presented to the emergency department with an episode of syncope. Physical examination demonstrated normal and regular heart sounds， and normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation. Echocardiogram described a well-circumscribed echo-dense mass in the right atrial cavity， which was attached to the septum but not obstructing the tricuspid annulus， measuring 1.7×2.2 cm at its widest di-ameter. Cardiac MRI revealed a mass with dark intensity which enhanced heterogeneously following intrave-nous administration of gadolinium-chelate， consistent with a myxoma. The location of this myxoma， coupled with the presence of a stalk allowing mobility， provides a clue to how this patient experienced transient ob-struction of the tricuspid valve leading to syncope.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Right heart tumors should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained syncope. Cardiac MRI with gadolinium-chelate administration can help differentiate this tumor from a right-sided atrial thrombus， which can pose a diagnostic challenge.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Cardiac Imaging Techniques · Heart Neoplasms·Myxoma· Syncope · Tricuspid Valve Myxomas are the most common primary tumor of the heart and right atrial myxoma accounts for 15-20% of cases with this tumor . Most of these are attached to the inter-atrial septum and are mostly asymptomatic but eventually can cause symptoms depending on the size， mobility， and location of the tumor . Syncope is a rare manifestation of right atrial myx-oma and its initial differentiation from a right atrial thrombus may be difficult. We present the case of an 89-year-old man with syncope who was found to have a right atrial myxoma.

【7】Case Report

【8】An 89-year-old man with a history of hypertension， hyperlip-idemia， chronic kidney disease stage 4， mild dementia， and benign prostatic hyperplasia presented to our emergency de-partment with an episode of syncope. He had a past histo-ry of positional syncope. Physical examination demonstrat-ed normal and regular heart sounds， and normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation. The syncope work-up including head computed tomography (CT)； carotid Doppler， electroen-cephalogram， electrocardiogram， and orthostatic blood pres-sure were negative.

【9】In the clinic， echocardiography described a well-circumscribed echo-dense mass in the right atrial cavity， attached to the septum but not obstructing the tricuspid annulus， measuring1.7×2.2cm at its widest diameter， consistent with either an atrial thrombus or an atrial myxoma.

【10】Cardiac MRI with gadolinium-chelate administration was con-ducted to further describe the mass. On cine bright blood steady-state free precession imaging， the mass was noted to be of dark intensity and it enhanced heterogeneously follow-ing intravenous administration of gadolinium-chelate， consis-tent with a myxoma . The freely mobile mass was attached with a thin stalk to the inferior-medial part of the tricuspid annulus near the ostium of the coronary sinus. The mass prolapsed freely into the tricuspid orifice during the cardiac cycle. Following the diagnosis of atrial myxoma， an-ticoagulation was considered but not started due to the pa-tients' history of recurrent falls. The patient was subsequent-ly lost to follow-up.

【11】Discussion

【12】The most common causes of syncope in the elderly are or-thostatic hypotension and reflex syncope (especially due to carotid sinus syndrome and cardiac arrhythmias)  and a cause is often not identified in the emergency room， especial-ly in the elderly. Diagnosis may be complicated by other con-founders of syncope (e.g.， distinguishing mechanical falls from syncope may be difficult in elderly patients). Other consider-ations are drug interactions and dehydration . The American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology Foundation Scientific Statement on the Evaluation of Syncope recommends that initial routine evaluation of the patient presenting with syncope should include careful history-taking， physical exam-ination (including orthostatic blood pressure evaluation)， and an electrocardiogram . Further evaluation is recommend-ed if a cause is not apparent after initial evaluation， and this includes echocardiography， an exercise test， and myocardial ischemia evaluation.

【13】Right heart tumors should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained syncope. Although right-sided myx-omas are rare， they may present with right heart failure sec-ondary to right ventricular outflow tract obstruction， or with syncope secondary to temporary complete obstruction of the tricuspid valve . The main factor predicting obstructive se-quelae is the tumor location. The location of this myxoma on the inferior-medial annulus of the tricuspid valve， coupled with the presence of a stalk allowing mobility， suggests why this pa-tient experienced transient obstruction of the tricuspid valve leading to syncope. In a related study evaluating the risk fac-tors for embolism in cardiac myxoma， location of the myxo-ma and irregular tumor surface were independently associated with increased risk of embolic complications . A diagnostic dilemma may arise in the differentiation of a thrombus from a myxoma. Echocardiography is useful in the initial evaluation of a cardiac mass. Although echocardiogram images could not be retrieved to aid in the pictorial assessment of the tumor lo-cation in this report， the cardiac MRI images that were includ-ed provided a detailed description of the tumor location and attachment. A particular advantage of cardiac MRI is that it can be used to distinguish a thrombus from a tumor by pro-viding more reliable tissue characterization. It is also better at assessing the relationship of a mass to cardiac structures . Myxomas usually originate from the inter-atrial septum； they can be pedunculated or sessile， and the contours are mostly smooth. Thrombi usually occupy the atrial appendage； they are broad-based and have irregular contours. In general， myx-omas， being vascular structures， tend to enhance with con-trast administration， while thrombi do not .

【14】Conclusions

【15】Right heart tumors should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained syncope. Cardiac MRI with gado-linium-chelate administration can help differentiate this tu-mor from a right-sided atrial thrombus， which can pose a di-agnostic challenge.

【0】Background： Hemangiomas are defined as benign soft tissue vascular tumors that are histologically classified as capillary cavernous， or mixed types. Hemangiomas can also be described based on clinical appearance as superficial， mixed， or deep lesions. Following a thorough search， only 3 case reports of superficial protruding lip mass were found in the literature. Other cases of tongue hemangioma have been reported in infants or young toddlers， and only rarely in adults.

【1】Case Reports： The first case was a 43-year-old pregnant woman， with an unremarkable medical and surgical history， in the second trimester who presented to the Otolaryngology Clinic with a chief concern of a progressively growing lesion， measuring 0.7x0.5 cm， over the lateral right side of the tongue for the last 2 weeks after accidentally biting her tongue during dinner. The second case was a 26-year-old woman with unremarkable medical and surgical history who presented to our Otolaryngology Clinic with a chief concern of a non-painful soft fungat-ing pink-red lip lesion 1.5x1 cm across the right lower lip growing for the last 4 months. This lesion appeared during the third trimester of pregnancy following a lip injury that was described as minor trauma.

【2】Conclusions： Although hemangiomas can occur anywhere on the body， they are most commonly found in the head and neck. These lesions are usually recognized quickly by patients and treating physicians and are thus clinically diag-nosed. Most vascular benign lesions regress on their own， but if detected early， they are surgically excised for cosmetic and functional reasons.

【3】Keywords： Rare oral tumors， Cavernous hemangioma， Vascular tumor

【4】Case 1

【5】A 26-year-old vitally stable healthy woman with an unre markable medical and surgical history presented to our Otolaryngology Clinic with concerns of a pink-red lower lip lesion that had been present for 4 months. The lesion was1.5x1 cm across the right lower lip and presented as a non-painful soft superficial fragile lesion .

【6】According to the patient， this lesion appeared during the third trimester of pregnancy following a lip injury that was described as minor trauma. The lesion grew slowly in size， and the pa-tient reported minor bleeding from it on occasion. There were no additional symptoms. The ear， nose， and throat examina-tion was routine. At the time， the most common differential diagnoses were traumatic fibroma and pyogenic granuloma. The decision was made to excise the lesion completely under local anesthesia in a well-equipped clinic， including diather-my in the event of bleeding. The lesion was excised complete ly and sutured with 5-0 vicryl rapide. The patient was given oral and topical antibiotics， with a follow-up appointment in a week .

【7】The pathology report revealed as capillary hemangioma，mak-ing it a rare presentation. One week after the excision， the pa-tient was seen with a healing wound， apart from a mild crust for which lubricants were prescribed.

【8】Case 2

【9】A 43-year-old vitally stable， healthy pregnant woman in her second trimester presented to the Otolaryngology Clinic with concerns of a progressively growing lesion on the tip of her tongue for the previous 2 weeks. The patient claims she be-came aware of the growing lesion only after accidentally bit-ing her tongue during dinner time. According to the patient， there was no previous history of similar lesions. There was no history of any other related symptoms.

【10】During physical examination， she was found to be vitally sta-ble， with a red fungated lesion measuring 0.7x0.5 cm over the lateral right sided of the tongue and no other lesions on the head and neck area .

【11】A monopolar excisional biopsy was performed， and the wound was left open for secondary intention healing， and the pa-tient was given oral analgesia and antibiotics. After 2 weeks of the procedure， she presented to the clinic with a complete-ly healed wound .

【12】The pathology report revealed an ulcerated capillary heman-gioma. She had a follow-up in our clinic 6 months later and showed no signs of local recurrence.

【13】Discussion

【14】Capillary hemangioma is a type of hamartoma that is distin-guished by vascular growth and endothelial cell proliferation. According to the literature， trauma can be linked to the de-velopment of some hemangiomas. Capillary hemangioma is difficult to diagnose because it is a rare presentation that fre-quently mimics pyogenic granuloma. Hemangioma prevalence can occur in childhood or later in life， with a female to male ratio of 3： 1 . During our review of the literature， we discov-ered only 3 cases of capillary hemangioma as a superficial lip mass . There were 2 male patients and 1 female patient among these cases. The lesion sites were the upper lip in 2 cas-es and the lower lip in 1 case. Two of patients in these cases were adults， and 1 was an adolescent. All patients had easily bleeding lesions in common. In addition， 1 patient， like ours， had a history of trauma. In none of the cases was radiological investigation used； instead， differential diagnosis was made based on clinical presentation. Capillary hemangioma appears in histopathology as capillaries with thin walls and little stro-ma. Hemangioma appears as unencapsulated red friable le-sions measuring from a single millimeter to several centime-ters in gross appearance. Treatment in our case was similar to that of the other cases reported in the literature， including complete surgical excision. During the follow-up periods for the cases， which were between 6 and 18 months， no recur-rence of the lesion was documented.

【15】Pyogenic granuloma are defined as rapidly growing peduncu-lated lobular capillary hemangiomas found most commonly on skin， gingiva， and oral mucosa. Although pyogenic granuloma demonstrates immunocytochemical and ultrastructural differ-ences， it is difficult to differentiate it from a hemangioma clin-ically . Capillary hemangioma frequently mimics pyogenic granuloma histopathologically but without inflammatory fea-tures， as it progresses from a densely cellular proliferation of endothelial cells in the early stages to a lobular mass of well-formed capillaries in the mature phase . Lingual hemangi-oma can present with a variety of clinical symptoms， ranging from asymptomatic to bleeding hemangiomas. Only a few cases of tongue hemangioma were discovered during our literature review for lingual hemangioma. Among these cases， the first reported hemangioma of the base of the tongue was in a male patient with a history of chronic irritation to the oral cavity with symptomatic presentation and an uncomplicated course. The second case was a 20-year-old pregnant woman diagnosed with cavernous hemangioma in 3 areas： her tongue， lips， and neck， with active bleeding that was managed with tracheosto-my at first， then arterial embolization and surgical excision .

【16】Treatment options include surgery， laser therapy， sclerosing agents， and embolization . Owing to the rapidly growing lesions causing cosmetic and functional concerns in both of our cases， surgical excision， the criterion standard treatment， was performed. In the first case， the lesion was completely ex-cised and sutured with 5-0 vicry. rapide under local anesthe-sia in a well-equipped clinic， including diathermy in the event of bleeding. In the second case， a monopolar excisional biop-sy was performed， and the wound was left open for second-ary intention healing. The relationship between hemangio-ma and pregnancy is not fully understood. However，research suggests that a high level of estrogen in pregnancy may play a potential role in mediating vascular growth and hemangi-oma formation . Both patients were followed up after their excisions and showed no signs of local recurrence. Using surgical excision in hemangioma can result in serious medical events， such as heavy bleeding. However， both patients were followed up after their excisions and showed no signs of lo-cal recurrence or bleeding.

【17】Conclusions

【18】Although hemangiomas can develop in any part of the body， the head and neck are most commonly affected. Because they are visible from the outside， these lesions are usually recognized quickly by patients and treating physicians and are thus clini-cally diagnosed. These vascular benign lesions usually regress on their own in most patients， but are surgically excised if they are detected early， for both cosmetic and functional reasons.

【0】Background：

【1】Steroids are used as anti-inflammatory agents， administered for a variety of medical conditions， either as short-or long-term treatment. Steroid use is associated with many adverse effects， including hyperglycemia， but keto-acidosis is rare.

【2】Case Report： We present the case of a 53-year-old woman who developed diabetic ketoacidosis after administration of meth-ylprednisolone during treatment of immune thrombocytopenic purpura. She did not have diabetes or a family history of diabetes. Steroid-induced hyperglycemia with insulin resistance， lipolysis， and ketogenesis occurred and were likely to have precipitated the ketoacidosis. Blood glucose， blood gases， and urine test results were diagnostic for ketoacidosis.

【3】Conclusions：

【4】The risk of ketoacidosis and hyperglycemia should be considered in the course of steroid therapy， even with-out a diagnosis of diabetes， especially in patients who have risk factors for diabetes mellitus including obesity and long-term use of steroids， so that early identification of diabetic ketoacidosis can prevent further morbid-ity and mortality in chronic patients.

【5】MeSH Keywords： Diabetic Ketoacidosis ·Glucocorticoids· Hyperglycemia·Purpura， Thrombocytopenic， Idiopathic·Steroids Steroids are considered the main treatment for many inflam-matory， immunologic， allergic， and malignant diseases， and they have numerous adverse effects on many organ systems， ranging from mild (e.g.， skin thinning and weight gain) to seri-ous life-threatening conditions (e.g.，serious infection， diabetes ketoacidosis \[DKA\]). A major adverse effect is hyperglycemia， which can worsen pre-existing diabetes or precipitate new di-abetes (steroid-induced diabetes)  through multifactorial mechanisms， including increased levels of hepatic glucocorti-coids， alteration of receptor function， glucose uptake inhibi-tion in adipose tissue， and abnormal carbohydrate metabo-lism， which lead to insulin resistance . Steroid-induced diabetes has been reported to occur in 1.5-27% of these pa-tients. The huge variation in incidence may be due to differ-ences in the studied populations， dose， and duration of steroid use， and even the diabetes definition used . The diabe-togenic effect of steroids is usually affected by dose-volume， duration of therapy， structure， and type of preparation ， older age (>65 years)， high HbA1c (>6.0%)， and low eGFR(<40 ml/min/1.73 m²). Longer steroids use (usually more than 21 days at a dose equivalent to >20 mg of prednisolone per day) increases risk of adverse effects， and patients with short-term use of steroids usually have no adverse effects or have only mild adverse effects .

【6】Diabetes ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute complication of hyper-glycemia， with high rates of morbidity and mortality. It is typ-ically characterized by serum glucose>250 mg/dL， PH <7.3， serum bicarbonate (HCO3) level <18 mEq/L， and elevated se-rum ketone level (ketonemia) and in urine (ketonuria)，elevat-ed anion gap >10， and dehydration . It is commonly as-sociated with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and it is less common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). It is more like-ly to affect people with T2DM who are experiencing extreme stress conditions like serious infection， myocardial infarctions， trauma， or other emergencies， as well as those taking medica-tions like atypical antipsychotics， glucagon， and steroids . To the best of our knowledge， there are few reported cases of steroid-induced DKA ， and the present case report is in-tended to fill this gap in the literature and to improve under-standing and management of this condition.

【7】Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired autoimmune disorder characterized by immune-mediated destruction of platelets in asymptomatic adults. It typically presents with isolated new-onset thrombocytopenia. It is defined as plate-let count <100×10/L due to destruction of platelets and in the absence of other causes of thrombocytopenia. There are 2types - primary (accounting for 80% of cases) without underly-ing causes， and secondary. Diagnosis of ITP is made only after other causes ofthrombocytopenia are ruled out. There are no specific tests for ITP， and bone marrow biopsy sometimes pro-vides only limited information . Hyperthyroidism has been reported among some patients with ITP (8-14%) ， and few cases have been reported as associated with T1DM  with co-existing systemic autoimmune disease. In a study of elderly ITP patients (age >60 years)， 22.2% (P 0.61) were dia-batic . First-line therapies are corticosteroids (e.g.， meth-ylprednisolone 30 mg/kg/day I for 5-7 days). Up to 85% of patients respond within 5 days， and maintenance oral corti-costeroids are required ， along with Ⅳ immunoglobulins(IVIG) 1 g/kg/day lV for 1-2 days . There is a report of 10patients with adverse events who had received multiple cycles of pulsed high-dose dexamethasone (as first-line alternative therapy for initial management of ITP)， with severe vomiting， transient hypertension， and steroid-induced diabetes and43.8% had to discontinue the steroid as ITP management due to adverse effects . We know of no case report of steroid-induced DKA in ITP patients.

【8】Case Report

【9】A 53-year-old woman with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) presented to our Emergency Department with gum bleeding occurring over the past 5 days. She had been discharged from the hospital 3 months ago after ITP flare on prednisolone ta-pering dose， but she discontinued the medication 1 month ago due to oral thrush. This time she presented to us with insidi-ous minimal self-limiting gum bleeding and epistaxis for the last 5 days. She also described gradually progressive polyuria， mainly nocturia， and polydipsia for 1 month. She reported she had gained about 3 kg body weight in the last 3 months. She reported no melena， vomiting， cough， headache， change in lev-el of consciousness， dizziness， chest pain， ecchymosis，local-ized weakness， fits， or hematuria/dysuria， and had no histo-ry of trauma or falling.

【10】Past medical and drug history： ITP has been diagnosed 11months ago in our hospital after we excluded all other possible causes. She had been admitted 2 times before， and this time she was admitted with active-controlled bleeding with severe thrombocytopenia. The last admission 3 months back was sim-ilar to the present admission， with a platelet count of 12x10°/L Initial steroids was given and she was discharged on 4th day with platelet count 25x10°/L and no complications during the hospital coarse； 2 readings of RBS were within normal limit， but HbAlc not done at that time. The discharge medication was a tapering dose of prednisolone over 6 weeks and con-tinue with a low dose until the next visit in 12 weeks， but she stopped taking this 5 weeks before the presentation because she had oral thrush and she missed the follow-up in the he-matology clinic. She was not taking any medication for the last4 weeks. She was not known to have diabetes， hypertension， or cardiac disease. She gave a history of check-up visits at an eye clinic 6 months ago， at which a full eye examination includ-ing fundoscopy was done and showed no evidence of acute or chronic problems (no retinopathy).

【11】Family History： No significant family history of diabetes.

【12】In the ER， she was fully conscious， oriented， not distressed， and appeared dehydrated. Her BMI was 35 kg/m?， with blood pres-sure 129/64 mmHg， pulse 110 beat/minute， respiration rate22 rates/min， 02 saturation 95% on ambient air， and temper-ature 36.9℃. Her oral cavity was moist， with no signs of ac-tive oozing， bleeding， or thrush. The chest was clear with equal air entry bilaterally. The abdomen was soft， lax， and without tenderness. No edema， swelling， redness， or tenderness were noted in the lower limbs.

【13】Her laboratory data at that time were： WBCs 9×10°/L， Hb12.6 g/L， platelets 1x10°/L， peripheral blood film showed sever thrombocytopenia，INR 1.05， PT 12 Secs， aPTT 30.2 Secs， Sodium135 mmol/L， potassium 4.2 mmol/L， chloride 92 mmol/L， cal-cium 8.9 mg/dL， RBS 551 mg/dL，phosphorus 4.5 mg/dL，mag-nesium 1.65 mg/dL， creatinine 1.26 mg/dL， urea 34.24 mg/dL， uric acid 6.1 mg/dL， total bilirubin 0.5 mg/dL， direct bilirubin0.32 mg/dL， albumin 3.7 g/dL， AST 17 U/L， ALT 6 U/L pH 7.48， pCO2 35， and HCO3 26.5. Urine analysis showed the following：glucose ++++， ketones +， and pus cells 2-5. The lipid profile was： cholesterol 158 mg/dL， HDL 36 mg/dL， LDL 98 mg/dL， tri-glyceride 118 mg/dL， and HbA1c 14.7. The thyroid profile was：TSH 0.21 mU/L FT4 14.6 mU/L FT3 3.24 mU/L， HBV NON-React， HCV NON-React， and HIV NON-React. An ECG showed sinus tachycardia， normal axis deviation， and no ischemic changes. A CT brain was normal study.

【14】She was admitted to the regular ward as a case of ITP flare with newly diagnosed of T2DM， and a plan for glucocorticoids， IVIG， and platelets transfusion for the ITP and insulin basal and slid-ing scale subcutaneous based on RBS reading for the diabetes.

【15】She received a total of 6 units of platelets transfusion， IV im-munoglobulin (IVIG)， and methylprednisolone 1 g lV daily for5 days.

【16】On day 1 she was evaluated by the primary team and was found to be anxious， vomiting， experiencing abdominal pain， confused， and looking ill. A random blood sugar was 465 mg/dL and venous blood gas was pH 7.26， pCO2 16， and HCO3 7.2. The platelet count was 7x10°/L. Troponin was normal and an ECG showed sinus tachycardia. A CT brain was repeated and showed no evidence of bleeding. Up to this time she had re-ceived the first dose of methylprednisolone. The Endocrine Team was consulted， and bolus lV fluids were started. Urine analysis showed glucose ++++ and ketones ++. In 1-hour the VBG was repeated， showing pH 7.1， HC3 3.2， anion gap (AG)27， and RBS 570. The DKA hospital protocol was initiated and the patient was moved to the ICU.

【17】On day 3， while she was in the ICU， she was found to be clini-cally stable， with improved conscious level and no active prob-lems. She had pH 7.31， pCO2 31.5， HCO3 16.5， and anion gap(AG) 10， so her DKA was resolved and she was moved back to the ward. Her platelet count was 32x10°/L.

【18】On day 6， she was discharged， as she was clinically improved， with no more bleeding since admission， and with platelet count 69x10°/L  and RBS 185 mg/dL， pH 7.4， pCO236， and HCO3 22.7.

【19】The discharge prescription was insulin glargine 26 units sub-cutaneous once daily， insulin glulisine 12 units subcutane-ous 3 times before meals， and metformin 500 mg TID to start with 500 mg daily for the first week and increase weekly to reach 1.5 gm once a day. She was followed up by Hematology， Endocrine， and the Diabetes Center.

【20】The patient was on close follow-up with the endocrinologist， and was evaluated 3 months after discharge. At that time， she was clinically stable， with improved general condition. Her platelet count was 132x10°/L and HbAlc was 9.3， although she was not strictly compliant with her medication. She was on the same management plan， but with more intense life-style modification and continued close follow-up. At 6-month post-discharge follow-up， the patient stated she had improved adherence to medication， with better glucose readings at home， weight reduction of 6 kg， and new BMI=27 kg/m²and HbA1c=6.9. A new plan was made to hold the insulin regimen and to continue metformin. During this time the patient was stable， with no active bleeding， no steroids， and no hospital admission， with baseline platelet count 100x10°/L

【21】Discussion

【22】We present the case of a 53-year-old woman who present-ed with persistent primary ITP that probably developed 3-12months before diagnosis. She responded to therapy， with no bleeding and platelet count >30x10/L. She had at least dou-bling of baseline platelet count measured on 2 occasions >7days  and no evidence of previous history of chronic di-abetes before using the steroids， as she was asymptomatic2 months ago)， and 2 readings of RBS within normal range(3 months ago). The eye examination results were normal(6 months ago). The absence of retinopathy in such a patient with steroid-induced diabetes suggests there had not been long periods of hyperglycemia . Unfortunately， there were no previous HbAlc results for this patient for comparison， which could be considered a limitation. Steroid-induced hyperglyce-mia is common in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. More and more reported cases of steroid-induced diabetes have odds ratios of 1.5-2.5， and this ratio can reach 10.34， with a hydrocortisone equivalent of >120 mg/day. High dosage and longer duration of steroids are strong predictors of diabetes. Also， other risk factors should be considered， such as age， over-weight， and sedentary lifestyle . The occurrence of DKA af-ter receiving steroids therapy is less common.

【23】The effects of systemic steroids on glucose metabolism are multifactorial and still not completely understood. The main mechanisms include increased glucose production via hepatic gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis， and more insulin resistance by reducing peripheral uptake at adipose and muscle level via inhibition of GLUT4 translocation . The acute effects of steroids are more distinct on glucose tolerance than is long-term use， and there is more risk of acute events of hypergly-cemia like DKA . Also，the pre-exposure status of patients with impaired glucose tolerance， especially those with high-risk factors of diabetes， is more pronounced to new-onset ste-roid-induced diabetes in such patients .

【24】Our patient had been on low-dose corticosteroid therapy as she was persistently ITP. During those times she developed steroid adverse effects (oral thrush， most likely candida in-fection) and stopped taking the medication. She started to have symptoms of hyperglycemia and was incidentally dis-covered in the ER to have diabetes with acute ITP. She was stable and non-critical， with uncontrolled hyperglycemia， so she was started on basal and sliding-scale insulin. Although she received a single dose of pulsed steroids， she developed acute DKA. Symptoms of hyperglycemia and elevated HbA1c means that the patient had previously experienced long peri-ods of hyperglycemia for at least 3 months. Although she did not have a significant family history of diabetes， confounding factors of obesity， genetics， and environmental factors may have played a role， along with the previous long-term use of steroids at her initial presentation of diabetes， which might have been triggered by the steroid therapy.

【25】Poor pre-discharge counseling about possible adverse effects of steroids in a patient receiving steroids for the first time， in addition to poor follow-up from the primary physician while a patient is on long-term steroids as an outpatient， are im-portant factors that contribute to adverse effects of steroids. demonstrating the need for more patient-centered care. Early detection and rapid intense management are crucial in acute DKA， especially in such a patient who needs close observa-tion， as the rapid deterioration in this case happened in a mat-ter of hours to days.

【26】Conclusions

【27】Steroids-induced hyperglycemia is quite common. Our case report emphasizes that DKA can be triggered by steroid ther-apy and extra attention is needed when steroids are initiated for ITP or chronic disorders. Patients with high-risk factors of diabetes， including obesity， family history of diabetes， chron-ic use of steroids， prediabetes， and other factors， should be even more concerning. Early detection and treatment can pre-vent further morbidity and mortality due to DKA.

【0】ABSTRACT Patients with CKD have an elevated likelihood of acquiring serious COVID-19. In comparison， the mortality rate tends to be higher than in the overall population and is not always specifically related to pulmonary compromise. This is not unexpected， considering that infectious or severe illnesses (e.g. influenza) are correlated with an elevated risk of cardiovascular problems in the overall population and individuals with CKD . In addition， CKD patients also have comorbidities with cardiovascular and diabetes that could be individually predisposed to extreme COVID-19.In the absence of a vaccine or licenced treatment， nephrologists should encourage CKD patients to follow guidelines for social exclusion targeted at high-risk patients. These should be applied to dialysis facilities， where a high suspicion index and COVID-19 monitoring should be added.

【1】KEYWORDS severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)， chronic kidney disease (CKD)， Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2(ACE2)， cytokine storm

【2】Introduction

【3】Situations had drastically altered since the first news of several instances of atypical pneumonia in China in December 2019 and the essential steps taken by the Chinese government to shut down the city of Wuhan (the subject of the issue). A novel coronavirus was identified as the causative agent of this res-piratory illness ， hit by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2)， and the disease was termed as coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) by the World Health Or-ganization . In 1966，Tyrell and Bynoe， who extracted viruses from patients with common colds， were first identified as coro-naviruses . They are enveloped， positive， single-stranded large RNA viruses that infect not just humans but also a wide variety of animals (bats， pangolins， cats， pigs and birds， among others). The size of the genome ranges between 26 and 32 kb. They were called coronaviruses， based on their morphology as spherical virions with a central shell and surface projections re-sembling a solar corona. Four subfamilies are known at present：a-，b-，c-and d-coronaviruses . SARS-CoV-2 is a member of the B b-coronavirus lineage and is closely related to SARS-CoV. Nucleocapsid protein (N)， spike protein (S)， small membrane protein (SM) and membrane glycoprotein (M) are coded by the key four structural genes， with specific membrane glycoprotein(HE) occurring in HCoV-OC43 and HKU1 b-coronaviruses . The clinical continuum of infection with COVID-19 is extremely complex， ranging from asymptomatic infection， anosmia，ageu-sia or mild upper respiratory tract disease to serious respiratory failure， pneumonia and even death . Diarrhoea， cutaneous and thrombotic symptoms have been identified recently . In elderly patients and those with chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease， hypertension or diabetes， more serious cases have been identified with increased mortality. However， in previously stable young patients， deaths have also resulted. It is predicted that patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at a greater risk of serious illness since their all-type infec-tion incidence and coronary disease prevalence are higher than the overall population. In CKD patients， pronounced improve-ments in the immune system have been identified， resulting in an immunosuppressed condition and recurrent infectious complications. Similarly， in CKD patients， chronic systemic in-flammation can also lead to higher morbidity and mortality. The pathogenicity of COVID-19， the persistent immuno-logical changes found in patients with CKD， and the risk of COVID-19 and the clinical consequences for patients with CKD are addressed in this study.

【4】Molecules associated kidney dysfunction in SARS-CoV-2 Infection

【5】A dynamic mechanism that remains enigmatic is the viral bind-ing， fusion， and eventual replication of coronavirus in targeted host cells. Even so， one synergistic action of S1 protein binding to receptors on the cell surface and a sequence of proteolysis were discovered to be necessary when the virus was attached to the cell surface. Scientists have estimated that at least three pro-teins， including Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2(ACE2)，type II transmembrane serine proteases (TMPRSS2) and an enzyme called furin are indispensably necessary for this phase. Interest-ingly， these molecules have been shown to be present in kidney tissue， indicating that the target cells attacked by SARS-CoV-2may be kidney tissue .

【6】Role of ACE2 in disease pathogenicity

【7】ACE2 belongs to the dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase class of angiotensin-converting enzymes and is homologous to the hu-man angiotensin-1-converting enzyme. ACE2 has been found to be one of the main receptors mediating the entrance of SARS-CoV-2 into human cells. Research performed by Fan and col-leagues  has shown that the levels of ACE2 mRNA and ACE2protein are also higher in renal cells. The spread of ACE2 expres-sions shows that the possible pathway of infection and direct kidney injury may be caused by SARS-CoV-2 binding to ACE2. Another research by Lin and colleagues based on single-cell analysis  also showed that ACE2 was enriched in proximal tubular cells， suggesting that the kidney is more vulnerable to SARS-CoV-2 infection.

【8】Previous experiments have indicated that in a number of renal tissue cells， ACE2 occurs. In the apical boundary of the proximal tubular cells， expression of ACE2 was highly positive， whereas it was less present in the cytoplasm. Visceral glomeru-lar stains were mild in ACE2， and mesangium and glomerular endothelium were negatives . Caibin Fan et al. have recently searched for literature and analyzed online datasets showing that the level of ACE2 protein expression is significantly greater in the kidney， particularly in renal tubular cells . It can be hypothesised that SARS-CoV-2 can impact the kidney directly by proximal renal tubular injury.

【9】Furin-Like Cleavage Site

【10】Earlier studies have shown that an unusual 'RRAR motif'in SARS-CoV-2 is a furin recognition site capable of being activated by an enzyme named furin . One of the most important distinctions between SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 is the motif-containing of this cleavage site between proteins S1/S2 . Furin is one of the proprotein convertases that can precisely cleave viral envelope glycoproteins， thus enhancing viral fusion into the membranes of host cells. Furin had a high level of expression in the salivary， lachrymal， intestine， liver， and even kidney glands . To date， by increasing the furin-mediated cleavage site， SARS-CoV-2 could use this particular function to become more contagious in the kidney and enhance kidney injury.

【11】Transmembrane Protease Serine 2

【12】Via binding the spike (S) proteins to ACE2 and S protein priming by host cell proteases， SARS-CoV-2 achieves access to a cell. Research performed by Hoffmann and colleagues  has shown that the ACE2 receptor is a SARS-CoV-2 cell receptor and that TMPRSS2 is an S protein priming cell protease， and both ACE2and TMPRSS2 are the central points of human cell infection with SARS-CoV-2. Both ACE2 and TMPRSS2 receptors occur in the kidney J. Which means that the virus is capable of targeting the kidney in this way? A TMPRSS2 inhibitor may also be beneficial for antiviral therapy， including kidney defence.

【13】Direct Virus Infection in Renal Tissue

【14】In the tubular epithelium and podocytes， clusters of coronavirus particles with distinctive spikes were observable under electron microscopic examination. Single-cell RNA sequencing technol-ogy provided cellular evidence that through the ACE2-related pathway， SARS-Cov-2 invaded human kidney tissue through the proximal convoluted tubule， proximal tubule， proximal straight tubule and glomerular parietal cells and used its cellular pro-tease TMPRSS2 for priming . These results revealed clear signs of SARS-CoV-2 penetration into the tissue of the kidneys. Renal target cells targeted by SARS-CoV-2 were also confirmed to be proximal renal tubular cells， compatible with the distri-bution of ACE2 in renal tissue . An up-regulation of the expression of ACE2 on the surface of renal tubular cells was also found. It is illustrated in figure 1.

【15】COVID-19 nephropathy due to cytokine storm in pa-tients

【16】A significant factor contributing to multiple organ injury in COVID-19 patients is also the cytokine wind. Highlevels of pro-inflammatory cytokines can cause heart， liver， and kidney shock and tissue damage， as well as respiratory failure or multiple organ failure . IL1B，IL1RA，IL7，IL8，IL9，IL10， FGF， GCSF， GMCSF， IFNy，IP10，MCP1，MIP1A，MIP1B，PDGF，TNFa， and VEGF were higher for both ICU patients and non-ICU patients than for healthy adults . ICU patients have an even higher degree of IL2， IL7， IL10， GCSF，IP10，MCP1，MIP1A， and TNFa relative to non-ICU patients. In most patients with extreme COVID-19， serum pro-inflammatory cytokines， including IL-6and IL-1B，IL-2，IL-8， IL-17， G-CSF，GM-CSF， IP10， MCP1，MIP1-af (also classified as CCL3)， and TNF were substantially elevated. Moreover， it was observed that the C-reactive protein and D-dimer were abnormally large. In 23 percent of ICU patients， acute kidney injury occurred， while acute kidney injury rarely occurs in non-ICU patients . This suggested that cytokine storm could be associated with kidney injury， and further studies are needed to explore the relationship between inflammatory storm and kidney injury.

【17】In addition to the direct SARS-CoV-2 virulence and cytokine storm， other causes， such as systematic hypoxia， pathological coagulation， and suspected drug-related or hyperventilation-related rhabdomyolysis， are potentially due to acute kidney

【18】Immune dysfunction in COVID 19 associated CKD

【19】SARS-CoV research revealed that AKI was the product of par-ticular pathogenic factors， such as cytokine release syndrome， rather than successful viral replication in the kidney in SARS patients. Flow cytometry was used to research the im-mune phenotype and the role of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in COVID-19 patients， taking into account the analogy be-tween SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 J. Studies have shown that lymphopenia has been documented in patients infected with SARS-CoV-2， mainly due to a significant reduction in ab-solute T cell counts， especially cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CD8+)， augmented neutrophil counts and enhanced proinflammatory cytokine levels. High interleukin (IL)-2， IL-6，IL-10 and inter-feron (IFN)-y levels were found in specific. It has therefore been hypothesised that loss of T cells during viral infection may con-tribute to increased inflammatory responses . It is known that T cells are necessary during viral infection to dampen over-active innate immune responses . In line with this theory， it has been found that the serum levels of IL-2， IL-4， IL-10， tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-af and interferon (IFN)-y reach their peaks when the T cell count decreases . Another significant result is higher serum concentrations of IL-6 and lower IFN-y than mod-erate variants in COVID-19 patients with more serious clinical manifestations. This is primarily attributed to the decline in lym-phocytes of CD4+，CD8+ and NK . The family of cytokines that play a critical role in innate immunity against viruses and other microbial pathogens is interferons (IFN). Binding to the IFN receptor triggers a cascade of gene activation signals coding for proteins with antiviral， antiproliferative or immunomodu-latory properties. The association between the IFN-Y and IL-6/sIL-6R signals normally leads to the mobilisation and eventual clearance of neutrophils， thereby regulating acute in-flammation infection and resolution and affecting the switch between innate and adaptive immunity . In patients infected with SARS-CoV-2， an improved cytokine storm can be associated with a higher IL-6/IFN-y ratio . These findings indicate that AKI may have an inflammatory aetiology induced by a cytokine storm in both SARS patients and patients with COVID-19. The cytokine storm is associated with an inflammatory mechanism that travels through the systemic circulation， starting at a local location. The inflammatory process， particularly when tissue oedema causes an increase in extravascular pressures and a con-sequent decrease in tissue perfusion， may cause organ dysfunc-tion. Corrective repair procedures start shortly after the onset of infection， and they can fully restore tissue and organ function in certain instances. However， when local tissue systems are injured by an extreme inflammatory disorder， healing happens with fibrosis， which may cause irreversible organ dysfunction. The immune system may not destroy SARS-CoV-2 when a cytokine storm happens， but it does kill vast numbers of normal cells and injure organs . In support of the hypothesis that AKI could be the product of inflammatory damage in COVID-19patients， the cohort study found that the kidney CT scan showed decreased density， suggestive of inflammation and oedema . Serious lung infections also require extended ventilatory assis-tance， in addition to being commonly associated with cytokine surge. The occurrence of sepsis， classically characterised by pro-nounced hypotension that involves treatment with inotropic medications， is predisposed to this. In patients with COVID-19 or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)， it is also possible that chronic inotropic-induced hypotension and vasoconstric-tion could be synonymous with glomerular filtrate decline and resulting in acute tubular necrosis . The theory of a multi-factorial aetiology of renal harm in COVID-19 is verified in the most recent research. Su et al.  showed pigmented casts with elevated levels of creatine phosphokinase， due to rhabdomyol-ysis， in an analysis carried out by examining autopsy kidney samples. In rhabdomyolysis， the huge release of myoglobin can cause kidney dysfunction due to muscle injury. In fact， myo-globin demonstrates its renal toxicity by various mechanisms：renal vasoconstriction associated with hypoperfusion-related hyperactivation of RASS and reduction of nitric oxide levels； de-velopment of intratubular casts； direct toxicity of renal tubular cells. Acute tubular necrosis occurs from these processes . Rhabdomyolysis is hypothetically multifactorial in COVID-19patients. In fact， tissue hypoxia due to hyperventilation or even to drug-induced damage can be secondary to the direct cytotoxic effect of SARS-CoV-2 on the muscle . Presumably， the patho-genesis of AKI could be implicated in COVID-19 patients that experience rhabdomyolysis. Numerous dependent mechanisms raise the risk of acute kidney injury in the COVID-19 setting are illustrated in figure 2.

【20】Thromboembolic events associated with disease pro-gression

【21】Recently， the high frequency of thromboembolic events in pa-tients with COVID-19 indicates that SARS-CoV-2 can play a significant role in coagulopathy induction. A condition of hy-percoagulability arose after examining the haematological pro-file of COVID-19 patients. In particular， high plasma levels of thrombocytopenia-associated reactive protein C， fibrinogen， D-dimer， and ferritin were observed in these patients . The formation of disseminated intravascular coagulation following SARS-CoV-2 infection has recently been verified by clinical and autopsy reports from China and the U.S. with evidence of mi-croangiopathy in multiple organs. In particular， the activation of COVID-19-associated macrophages， the cytokine storm and the damage-associated molecular proteins will induce the release of both tissue factors and the activation of hypercoagulability-predisposing coagulation factors. In some instances， the progres-sion of acute tubular necrosis into cortical necrosis and hence the development of permanent renal injury may be favoured by this state of hypercoagulability. These findings indicate that， in some supportive COVID-19 patients， low back pain and mi-crohematuria observed could be signs of renal infarction . The contribution of SARS-CoV-2 to CKD production could in-clude pathways close to those defined for acute kidney injury. Indeed， a non-trivial portion of patients has been found to de-velop symptoms of tubular or glomerular disruption during the infection. Due to the virus， direct tubule-glomerular cell damage frequently presents with proteinuria and hematuria， which could， in turn， initiate a chronic， non-reversible process. Proteinuria has been shown to have a direct toxic impact on renal tubular cells and， over time， induce renal fibrosis . In conclusion， the renal damage found in patients with COVID-19 is the product of complex pathways directly and indirectly caused by SARS-CoV-2 predisposing patients to renal dysfunc-tion. To better understand the pathophysiological pathways of kidney injury， to establish new clinical approaches capable of minimizing and/or preventing kidney damage and to improve the prognosis of patients with COVID-19， further studies are required.

【22】Clinical Features in Patients with Chronic Kidney Dis-ease (CKD)

【23】The increased risk of serious COVID-19 infection and mortality appears to be associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The correlation between markers of renal dysfunction and death in a cohort of 701 COVID-19 patients was examined by Cheng et al. They found that in 14.4% and 13.1% of patients， 43.9% of patients admitted had proteinuria， and 26.7% had hematuria.In14.4% and 13.1% of patients， serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels were increased. In 13.1 percent of patients， the average glomerular filtration rate was < 60 mL/min per

【24】1.73 m2 . In general， the authors found that the prevalence of proteinuria was correlated with 4 to 11 times the risk of in-hospital death relative to COVID-19 patients without kidney damage in the univariate study. At the same time， hematuria enhanced the risk of death by 12 times. These hazard ratios (HR) were higher than threat factors such as advanced age (HR： 2.43)， serious disease (HR： 6.10) and remained positively linked with mortality even after adaptation (thus multivariate analysis) by age， gender， the seriousness of the disease， lymphocyte count， comorbidity， indicating that kidney damage measures play a crucial role in assessing the prognosis of COVID-19 . In general， the authors found that the prevalence of proteinuria was correlated with 4 to 11 times the risk of in-hospital death relative to COVID-19 patients without kidney damage in the univariate study hematuria enhanced the risk of death by 12times. These hazard ratios (HR) were higher than threat factors such as advanced age (HR： 2.43)， serious disease (HR： 6.10) and remained positively linked with mortality even after adaptation(thus multivariate analysis) by age， gender， the seriousness of the disease，lymphocyte count， comorbidity， indicating that kidney damage measures play a crucial role in assessing the prognosis of COVID-19. A significant proportion of COVID-19 patients have recently been shown to suffer from other comorbidities， and the majority of these patients are also elderly and male . Among these comorbidities， an individual risk variable for poor prognosis is the involvement of chronic kidney disease.

【25】On the contrary， it is also true that nephropathic patients are mostly affected by hypertension and cardiovascular disease per se， which can contribute to a greater risk of complications with COVID-19 relative to the general public or patients without the renal disease . Patients with cardiovascular disease consid-ered a biomarker of an elevated risk of COVID 19 infection are also nephropathic patients . However， patients infected with other viruses such as the H1N1 flu virus and who developed kidney injury during infection were found to have an elevated chance of death， around 3-8 times， relative to those who did not. In addition， patients with elevated serum creatinine levels entering the hospital were overwhelmingly male and older (me-dian age 73 years). They were more critically ill than patients with normal serum creatinine (median age was 61 years).

【26】In comparison， patients with elevated baseline serum cre-atinine levels have improved leukocyte count with a rise in total leukocyte count and a reduction in the amount of lym-phocytes and platelets. Abnormalities of the coagulation path-way， including extended activated partial thromboplastin du-ration and higher D-dimer， are more common in patients with elevated creatinine baseline serum levels. The prevalence of procalcitonin-increased patients and the plasma levels of aspar-tate aminotransferase and LDH in patients with CKD are both higher relative to those with normal renal function. The fre-quency of in-hospital mortality was observed to be considerably higher in CKD patients than in those patients with typical base-line creatinine serum levels.
